verses.1:1: And it happened after the death of Moses, the servant of the Lord, that the Lord spoke to Joshua, the son of Nun, the attendant of Moses, and said to him:
verses.1:2: "Moses My servant is dead. Rise, and cross this Jordan, you and all the people with you, into the land that I will give to the sons of Israel.
verses.1:3: Every place that the sole of your foot treads on, I will deliver to you, just as I spoke to Moses.
verses.1:4: From the desert and Lebanon as far as the great river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites as far as the great sea toward the setting of the sun will be your boundary.
verses.1:5: No one will be able to resist you all the days of your life; just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not let you go, nor will I abandon you.
verses.1:6: Be strong and resolute, for you will divide by lot to this people the land for which I swore to their fathers that I would deliver it to them.
verses.1:7: Be strong, therefore, and very resolute, so that you may keep and carry out all the law that Moses My servant commanded you. Do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left, so that you may understand all that you do.
verses.1:8: Let the scroll of this law not depart from your mouth, but you will meditate on it day and night, so that you may keep and carry out everything that is written in it; then you will direct your way, and you will understand it.
verses.1:9: Look, I command you: be strong and resolute. Do not dread, and do not fear, because the Lord your God is with you in all things, wherever you may go."
verses.1:10: And Joshua commanded the leaders of the people, saying, "Pass through the middle of the camp, and order the people, and say:
verses.1:11: 'Prepare provisions for yourselves, because after the third day you will cross the Jordan, and you will enter to possess the land that the Lord your God is about to give to you.'"
verses.1:12: To the Reubenites also, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, he said:
verses.1:13: "Remember the word that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you, saying, 'The Lord your God has given you rest, and all the land.'
verses.1:14: Your wives, and children, and livestock will remain in the land that Moses delivered to you beyond the Jordan; but you, cross over armed ahead of your brothers, all who are strong of hand, and fight for them,
verses.1:15: until the Lord gives rest to your brothers, just as He also gave to you, and they themselves also possess the land that the Lord your God is about to give to them; and so return to the land of your possession, and you will live in it, the land that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave to you beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun."
verses.1:16: And they answered Joshua and said, "Everything that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
verses.1:17: Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will also obey you; only may the Lord your God be with you, just as He was with Moses.
verses.1:18: Whoever contradicts your mouth and does not obey all the words that you command him, let him die. Only be strong yourself, and act courageously."
verses.2:1: Therefore Joshua, the son of Nun, sent two men from Shittim as spies in secret, and said to them, "Go and inspect the land, and the city of Jericho." Going on, they entered the house of a woman who was a prostitute, named Rahab, and rested at her house.
verses.2:2: And it was reported to the king of Jericho, and said, "Look, men from the sons of Israel have come in here by night to spy out the land."
verses.2:3: And the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, for indeed they are spies, and they have come to inspect all the land."
verses.2:4: And taking the men, the woman hid them and said, "I admit it, they came to me, but I did not know where they were from;
verses.2:5: and when the gate was being closed in the darkness, they also went out at the same time; I do not know where they went. Pursue them quickly, and you will catch them."
verses.2:6: But she herself had made the men go up onto the rooftop of her house, and had covered them with the stalks of flax that were there.
verses.2:7: Now those who had been sent followed them along the road that leads to the ford of the Jordan; and when they had gone out, the gate was immediately closed.
verses.2:8: Those who were hiding had not yet fallen asleep, and look, the woman went up to them and said:
verses.2:9: "I know that the Lord has delivered the land to you, for indeed terror of you has fallen upon us, and all the inhabitants of the land have grown faint.
verses.2:10: We have heard that the Lord dried up the waters of the Red Sea at your entry, when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you killed.
verses.2:11: And hearing these things, we were greatly afraid, and our heart grew faint, nor did any spirit remain in us at your entry; for the Lord your God, He Himself is God in heaven above and on earth below.
verses.2:12: Now therefore, swear to me by the Lord that just as I have acted with mercy toward you, so you also will act toward the house of my father, and give me a true sign,
verses.2:13: that you will save my father and mother, and my brothers and sisters, and everything that belongs to them, and rescue our lives from death."
verses.2:14: They answered her, "May our life be for you to death, provided only that you do not betray us; and when the Lord delivers the land to us, we will act with mercy and truth toward you."
verses.2:15: So she let them down by a rope from the window, for her house was attached to the wall.
verses.2:16: And she said to them, "Climb up to the hill country, so that those returning may not happen to encounter you, and stay hidden there for three days until they return; and then you will go on your way."
verses.2:17: They said to her, "We will be guiltless of this oath by which you made us swear,
verses.2:18: if, as we enter the land, this scarlet cord is a sign, and you tie it in the window through which you let us down, and you gather your father and mother, and your brothers and all your relatives, into your house.
verses.2:19: Whoever goes out the door of your house, his own blood will be on his head, and we will be clear. But the blood of all who are with you in the house will fall back on our head if anyone touches them.
verses.2:20: However, if you choose to betray us and bring this matter out into the open, we will be free from this oath by which you made us swear."
verses.2:21: And she answered, "Just as you have spoken, so let it be." And sending them away so that they might go on, she hung the scarlet cord in the window.
verses.2:22: Now walking on, they reached the hill country and remained there three days, until those who had pursued them returned; for searching all along the road, they did not find them.
verses.2:23: When those men had entered the city, the spies turned back and came down from the mountain; and having crossed the Jordan, they came to Joshua, the son of Nun, and recounted to him everything that had happened to them,
verses.2:24: and said, "The Lord has delivered all this land into our hands, and all its inhabitants are laid low with fear."
verses.3:1: Therefore Joshua, rising in the night, moved the camp; and going out from Shittim, he himself and all the sons of Israel came to the Jordan, and they stayed there three days.
verses.3:2: When these had elapsed, the heralds passed through the middle of the camp,
verses.3:3: and began to call out, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and the priests of the Levitical lineage carrying it, you also rise up and follow those going ahead;
verses.3:4: and let there be between you and the ark a space of two thousand cubits, so that you may be able to see from a distance and know by which road you should go, because you have not walked along it before; and take care that you do not approach the ark."
verses.3:5: And Joshua said to the people, "Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you."
verses.3:6: And he said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and go ahead of the people." Fulfilling the orders, they took it up and walked ahead of them.
verses.3:7: And the Lord said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to exalt you before all Israel, so that they may know that just as I was with Moses, so I am also with you.
verses.3:8: As for you, command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, and say to them, 'When you have entered part of the water of the Jordan, stand in it.'"
verses.3:9: And Joshua said to the sons of Israel, "Come near here, and hear the word of the Lord your God."
verses.3:10: And again, "By this," he said, "you will know that the Lord, the living God, is in your midst, and He will destroy in your sight the Canaanite and the Hittite, the Hivite and the Perizzite, the Girgashite also and the Jebusite, and the Amorite.
verses.3:11: Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth will go ahead of you through the Jordan.
verses.3:12: Prepare twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one for each tribe.
verses.3:13: And when the priests who carry the ark of the Lord God of the whole earth place the soles of their feet in the waters of the Jordan, the waters that are lower will flow down and fail, while those that come from above will stand still in one mass."
verses.3:14: Therefore the people went out from their tents to cross the Jordan, and the priests who were carrying the ark of the covenant went on ahead of them.
verses.3:15: And when they had entered the Jordan, and their feet had been dipped in part of the water (for the Jordan had filled the banks of its channel at the time of harvest),
verses.3:16: the descending waters stood still in one place, and swelling up like a mountain, they appeared from a distance, from the city that is called Adam as far as the place Zarethan; while those that were lower went down into the Sea of the Wilderness (which is now called the Dead Sea), until they failed completely.
verses.3:17: Meanwhile the people marched opposite Jericho, and the priests who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood ready on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, and all the people were crossing through the dried-up channel.
verses.4:1: When they had crossed over, the Lord said to Joshua:
verses.4:2: "Choose twelve men, one from each tribe,
verses.4:3: and command them to take up from the middle of the riverbed of the Jordan, where the feet of the priests stood, twelve very hard stones, which you shall set in the place of the camp where you pitch tents tonight."
verses.4:4: And Joshua called the twelve men whom he had chosen from the sons of Israel, one from each tribe,
verses.4:5: and said to them, "Go before the ark of the Lord your God to the middle of the Jordan, and carry from there one stone each on your shoulders, according to the number of the sons of Israel,
verses.4:6: so that it may be a sign among you; and when your children ask you tomorrow, saying, 'What do these stones mean?'
verses.4:7: you shall answer them, 'The waters of the Jordan failed before the ark of the covenant of the Lord when it crossed over it; for this reason these stones have been set as a memorial for the sons of Israel forever.'"
verses.4:8: Therefore the sons of Israel did just as Joshua commanded them, carrying twelve stones from the middle of the riverbed of the Jordan, as the Lord had ordered him, according to the number of the sons of Israel, all the way to the place where they encamped, and they set them there.
verses.4:9: Joshua also set twelve other stones in the middle of the riverbed of the Jordan, where the priests who were carrying the ark of the covenant stood; and they are there until the present day.
verses.4:10: Now the priests who were carrying the ark remained standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything was completed that the Lord had commanded Joshua to speak to the people, and that Moses had told him. And the people hurried and crossed over.
verses.4:11: And when all had crossed over, the ark of the Lord also crossed over, and the priests proceeded before the people.
verses.4:12: The sons of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh also went ahead of the sons of Israel armed, just as Moses had commanded them;
verses.4:13: and forty thousand warriors, by squadrons and columns, marched across the flatlands and plains of the city of Jericho.
verses.4:14: On that day the Lord magnified Joshua before all Israel, so that they feared him just as they had feared Moses while he was still alive.
verses.4:16: "Command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant to come up from the Jordan."
verses.4:17: And he commanded them, saying, "Come up from the Jordan."
verses.4:18: And when those carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord had come up and had begun to tread on dry ground, the waters returned to their riverbed and flowed just as they had been accustomed to before.
verses.4:19: Now the people came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped at Gilgal opposite the eastern side of the city of Jericho.
verses.4:20: The twelve stones also, which they had taken from the riverbed of the Jordan, Joshua set at Gilgal,
verses.4:21: and said to the sons of Israel, "When your children ask their fathers tomorrow and say to them, 'What do these stones mean?'
verses.4:22: you shall teach them and say, 'Across the dry riverbed Israel crossed this Jordan,
verses.4:23: as the Lord your God dried up its waters in your sight until you crossed over,
verses.4:24: just as He had done earlier in the Red Sea, which He dried up until we crossed over,
verses.4:25: so that all the peoples of the lands may learn the most mighty hand of the Lord, so that you also may fear the Lord your God at all times.'"
verses.5:1: Therefore, after all the kings of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan on the western side, and all the kings of Canaan who possessed the places near the great sea, heard that the Lord had dried up the streams of the Jordan before the sons of Israel until they crossed over, their heart melted, and no spirit remained in them, as they feared the entrance of the sons of Israel.
verses.5:2: At that time the Lord said to Joshua, "Make for yourself stone knives, and circumcise the sons of Israel a second time."
verses.5:3: He did what the Lord had commanded, and circumcised the sons of Israel on the hill of the foreskins.
verses.5:4: Now this is the reason for the second circumcision: all the people of the male sex who came out of Egypt, all the fighting men, died in the desert along the very long circuits of the way,
verses.5:5: all of whom were circumcised. But the people who were born in the desert
verses.5:6: were uncircumcised during the forty years of the journey through the very vast wilderness, until those were consumed who had not listened to the voice of the Lord, and to whom He had previously sworn that He would not show them a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.5:7: Their sons succeeded to the place of their fathers, and were circumcised by Joshua, because, just as they had been born, they still had their foreskin, and no one had circumcised them on the way.
verses.5:8: Now after they were all circumcised, they remained in the same place of the camp until they were healed.
verses.5:9: And the Lord said to Joshua, "Today I have taken away the reproach of Egypt from you." And the name of that place was called Gilgal, until the present day.
verses.5:10: And the sons of Israel remained at Gilgal, and kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month toward evening in the plains of Jericho;
verses.5:11: and they ate of the produce of the land on the next day, unleavened loaves and parched grain of the same year.
verses.5:12: And the manna ceased after they ate of the produce of the land, nor did the sons of Israel use that food any longer, but they ate of the produce of the present year of the land of Canaan.
verses.5:13: Now when Joshua was in the field of the city of Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and saw a man standing opposite him, holding a drawn sword; and he went over to him and said, "Are you ours, or of our adversaries?"
verses.5:14: He answered, "Not at all, but I am the commander of the army of the Lord, and now I come."
verses.5:15: Joshua fell face down to the ground, and bowing in homage, he said, "What does my lord speak to his servant?"
verses.5:16: "Loosen your sandal from your feet," he said, "for the place on which you are standing is holy." And Joshua did as he had been ordered.
verses.6:1: Now Jericho was shut and fortified out of fear of the sons of Israel, and no one dared to go out or come in.
verses.6:2: And the Lord said to Joshua, "Look, I have given Jericho into your hand, and its king, and all the mighty men.
verses.6:3: Circle the city, all you fighting men, once a day; thus you shall do for six days.
verses.6:4: But on the seventh day, let the priests take up seven trumpets that are used in the jubilee and go ahead of the ark of the covenant; you will circle the city seven times, and the priests will blow the trumpets.
verses.6:5: And when the sound of the trumpet resounds, longer and more broken, and rings out in your ears, all the people shall shout together with a very great outcry, and the walls of the city will collapse to their foundations, and each one shall enter through the place opposite which he stands."
verses.6:6: Therefore Joshua the son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven other priests take up seven jubilee horns and march before the ark of the Lord."
verses.6:7: To the people also he said, "Go and circle the city, armed, going ahead of the ark of the Lord."
verses.6:8: And when Joshua had finished his words, and the seven priests were sounding the seven horns before the ark of the covenant of the Lord,
verses.6:9: and the whole armed army was going ahead, the rest of the crowd followed the ark, and everything resounded with the horns.
verses.6:10: Now Joshua had commanded the people, saying, "You shall not shout, nor shall your voice be heard, nor shall any word go out from your mouth, until the day comes on which I say to you, 'Shout, and cry out.'"
verses.6:11: Therefore the ark of the Lord circled the city once during the day, and returned to the camp and remained there.
verses.6:12: Therefore, as Joshua rose during the night, the priests took up the ark of the Lord,
verses.6:13: and seven of them seven horns that are used in the jubilee; and they went ahead of the ark of the Lord, walking and sounding them, and the armed people went before them, while the rest of the crowd followed the ark and resounded with the horns.
verses.6:14: And they circled the city once on the second day and returned to the camp. Thus they did for six days.
verses.6:15: But on the seventh day, rising at dawn, they circled the city, as had been arranged, seven times.
verses.6:16: And when on the seventh circuit the priests sounded the horns, Joshua said to all Israel, "Cry out aloud, for the Lord has delivered the city to you.
verses.6:17: And let this city, and everything that is in it, be anathema to the Lord; only Rahab the prostitute shall live, with all who are with her in the house, for she hid the messengers whom we sent.
verses.6:18: But you, take care not to touch anything of these things that have been commanded, so that you may not be guilty of transgression, and the whole camp of Israel may not be under sin and be troubled.
verses.6:19: But whatever gold and silver there is, and bronze vessels and iron, shall be consecrated to the Lord, stored up in His treasuries."
verses.6:20: Therefore, as all the people cried out aloud and the trumpets sounded, after the voice and sound rang out in the ears of the multitude, the walls immediately collapsed, and each one went up through the place that was opposite him, and they captured the city,
verses.6:21: and they killed everything that was in it, from man to woman, from infant to old man. They also struck down oxen and sheep and donkeys with the edge of the sword.
verses.6:22: Now Joshua said to the two men who had been sent as spies, "Enter the house of the prostitute woman, and bring her out, and everything that belongs to her, just as you confirmed to her by an oath."
verses.6:23: And the young men went in and brought out Rahab, and her parents, her brothers also, and all her household goods and her relatives, and made them remain outside the camp of Israel.
verses.6:24: But the city, and everything that was in it, they set on fire, except for the gold and silver, and the bronze vessels and iron, which they consecrated into the treasury of the Lord.
verses.6:25: However, Joshua kept alive Rahab the prostitute, and her father's household, and everything that she had, and they lived in the midst of Israel until the present day, because she hid the messengers whom he had sent to spy out Jericho. At that time Joshua pronounced a curse, saying:
verses.6:26: "Cursed before the Lord be the man who raises up and builds the city of Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn may he lay its foundations, and at the cost of the youngest of his children may he set its gates."
verses.6:27: Therefore the Lord was with Joshua, and his name was spread throughout all the land.
verses.7:1: But the sons of Israel violated the command and appropriated some of what was devoted to destruction. For Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took something from what was devoted to destruction, and the Lord became angry against the sons of Israel.
verses.7:2: And when Joshua sent men from Jericho against Ai, which is beside Beth-aven on the eastern side of the town of Bethel, he said to them, "Go up and scout the land." Carrying out the commands, they scouted Ai.
verses.7:3: And when they returned, they said to him, "Do not let all the people go up, but let two or three thousand men go and wipe out the city. Why should all the people be worn out in vain against so very few enemies?"
verses.7:4: So three thousand fighting men went up. Immediately turning their backs,
verses.7:5: they were struck down by the men of the city of Ai, and thirty-six men among them fell. And the adversaries pursued them from the gate as far as Shebarim, and they fell while fleeing down the slopes; and the heart of the people grew terrified and melted like water.
verses.7:6: Then Joshua tore his garments and fell face down to the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, both he and all the elders of Israel, and they threw dust on their heads.
verses.7:7: And Joshua said, "Ah, Lord God, why did You wish to lead this people across the Jordan River, to hand us over into the hands of the Amorite and destroy us? If only we had remained across the Jordan, just as we began!
verses.7:8: My Lord God, what shall I say, seeing Israel turning its back to its enemies?
verses.7:9: The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear, and massing together as one, they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. And what will You do for Your great name?"
verses.7:10: And the Lord said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you lying face down on the ground?
verses.7:11: Israel has sinned and has violated My covenant; they have taken from what was devoted to destruction, and have stolen and lied, and have hidden it among their belongings.
verses.7:12: And Israel will not be able to stand before its enemies, and it will flee from them, because it has been defiled by what was devoted to destruction. I will not be with you any longer until you crush the one who is guilty of this crime.
verses.7:13: Get up, sanctify the people, and say to them, 'Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow, for this is what the Lord God of Israel says: "What is devoted to destruction is in your midst, Israel; you will not be able to stand before your enemies until the one who is contaminated by this crime is wiped out from among you."
verses.7:14: And in the morning you shall come forward one by one by your tribes; and whichever tribe the lot finds shall come forward by its clans, and the clan by households, and the household by men.
verses.7:15: And whoever he may be who is caught in this misdeed shall be burned with fire along with all his property, because he has violated the covenant of the Lord and has committed an outrage in Israel.'"
verses.7:16: So Joshua rose in the morning and brought Israel forward by its tribes, and the tribe of Judah was found.
verses.7:17: When it had been presented according to its families, the family of Zerah was found. Presenting that family also by households, he found Zabdi.
verses.7:18: And dividing his household into individual men, he found Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah.
verses.7:19: And Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the Lord God of Israel and confess, and tell me what you have done; do not hide it."
verses.7:20: And Achan answered Joshua and said to him, "Truly I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and in this manner and that I have done.
verses.7:21: For I saw among the spoils a very fine scarlet cloak, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a golden bar of fifty shekels; and coveting them, I carried them off and hid them in the ground at the middle of my tent, and I covered the silver with dug-up earth."
verses.7:22: So Joshua sent attendants, who ran to his tent and discovered everything hidden in that same place, together with the silver.
verses.7:23: Removing them from the tent, they brought them to Joshua and to all the sons of Israel, and threw them down before the Lord.
verses.7:24: Therefore Joshua took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, the cloak, and the golden bar, his sons also and his daughters, the oxen, donkeys, and sheep, the tent itself, and all the household goods (and all Israel was with him), and they led them to the Valley of Achor,
verses.7:25: where Joshua said, "Because you have troubled us, may the Lord utterly trouble you on this day." And all Israel stoned him, and everything that belonged to him was consumed by fire.
verses.7:26: And they gathered over him a great heap of stones, which remains until the present day. And the fury of the Lord turned away from them. And the name of that place has been called the Valley of Achor until today.
verses.8:1: Then the Lord said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid, and do not be terrified; take with you the entire multitude of fighting men, and rising up, go up against the town of Ai. Look, I have handed over into your hand its king and people, and the city and the land.
verses.8:2: And you shall do to the city of Ai and to its king just as you did to Jericho and to its king; however, you shall seize the plunder and all the animals for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city behind it."
verses.8:3: And Joshua rose up, and the entire army of warriors with him, to go up against Ai; and he sent thirty thousand chosen valiant men by night,
verses.8:4: and commanded them, saying, "Set an ambush behind the city, and do not withdraw too far; and you shall all be ready.
verses.8:5: But I and the rest of the multitude that is with me will advance from the opposite side against the city. And when they come out against us, just as we did before, we will flee and turn our backs,
verses.8:6: until in pursuing us they are drawn far away from the city; for they will think that we are fleeing just as before.
verses.8:7: Therefore, while we flee and they pursue, you shall rise up from the ambush and lay waste to the city; and the Lord your God will hand it over into your hands.
verses.8:8: And when you have captured it, set fire to it, and so you shall do everything as I have ordered."
verses.8:9: And he sent them away, and they went to the place of the ambush and stayed between Bethel and Ai, on the western side of the city of Ai; but Joshua remained that night in the midst of the people,
verses.8:10: and rising at daybreak, he mustered his companions and went up with the elders at the front of the army, surrounded by the support of fighting men.
verses.8:11: And when they had come and gone up opposite the city, they took their stand on the northern side of the city, with an intervening valley between it and them.
verses.8:12: Now he had chosen five thousand men and placed them in ambush between Bethel and Ai on the western side of that same city;
verses.8:13: but all the rest of the army drew up its battle line to the north, so that the rearmost of that multitude reached the western side of the city. Therefore Joshua went away that night and stood in the middle of the valley.
verses.8:14: When the king of Ai saw this, he hurried in the morning and went out with the entire army of the city, and drew up his battle line facing the desert, not knowing that an ambush lay hidden behind his back.
verses.8:15: Then Joshua and all Israel gave ground, feigning fear and fleeing along the way of the wilderness.
verses.8:16: And they, shouting out together and urging one another on, pursued them. And when they had withdrawn from the city,
verses.8:17: and not even one had remained in the city of Ai and Bethel who was not pursuing Israel (just as they had burst out, leaving the towns open),
verses.8:18: the Lord said to Joshua, "Raise the shield that is in your hand toward the city of Ai, for I will hand it over to you."
verses.8:19: And when he had raised the shield opposite the city, the men in ambush, who lay hidden, rose up immediately, and going to the city, they captured and set fire to it.
verses.8:20: Now the men of the city who were pursuing Joshua, looking back and seeing the smoke of the city rising all the way to the sky, were no longer able to flee this way or that, especially since those who had feigned flight and were heading toward the wilderness had resisted the pursuers most strongly.
verses.8:21: And Joshua and all Israel, seeing that the city had been captured and that the smoke of the city was rising, turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
verses.8:22: Indeed, those also who had captured and set fire to the city, coming out of the city toward their own men, began to strike the enemy in the middle. Therefore, while the adversaries were being cut down from both sides, so that no one from so great a multitude was saved,
verses.8:23: they also seized the king of the city of Ai alive and presented him to Joshua.
verses.8:24: Therefore, when all those who had pursued Israel as it headed toward the desert had been killed and had fallen by the sword in that same place, the sons of Israel turned back and struck down the city.
verses.8:25: Now those who had fallen on that same day, from man to woman, were twelve thousand people, all of the city of Ai.
verses.8:26: Joshua, however, did not withdraw his hand, which he had extended upward while holding the shield, until all the inhabitants of Ai were killed.
verses.8:27: However, the sons of Israel divided the livestock and the plunder of the city among themselves, just as the Lord had commanded Joshua.
verses.8:28: And he set fire to the city and made it an everlasting mound.
verses.8:29: He also hanged its king on a gibbet until evening and the setting of the sun. And Joshua gave the command, and they took his corpse down from the cross and threw it down at the very entrance of the city, piling over him a great heap of stones, which remains until the present day.
verses.8:30: Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord God of Israel on Mount Ebal,
verses.8:31: just as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded the sons of Israel, and as is written in the scroll of the law of Moses: an altar of unpolished stones, which iron had not touched; and he offered burnt offerings on it to the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings.
verses.8:32: And he wrote on the stones the Deuteronomy of the law of Moses, which he had set down before the sons of Israel.
verses.8:33: And all the people, and the elders, and the leaders and judges, were standing on both sides of the ark, in the sight of the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the foreigner as well as the native. Half of them were near Mount Gerizim, and half near Mount Ebal, just as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded. And first indeed he blessed the people of Israel.
verses.8:34: After these things he read all the words of blessing and cursing, and all things that had been written in the scroll of the law.
verses.8:35: He left nothing untouched of those things that Moses had commanded, but repeated everything before the entire multitude of Israel, the women and little children, and the foreigners who stayed among them.
verses.9:1: When these things were heard, all the kings beyond the Jordan, who lived in the hill country and the plains, in the coastal regions and on the shore of the great sea, and those also who lived near Lebanon, the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite,
verses.9:2: gathered together as one to fight against Joshua and Israel with one mind and the same resolve.
verses.9:3: But those who lived in Gibeon, hearing all that Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
verses.9:4: and planning craftily, took provisions for themselves, putting old sacks on donkeys, and wineskins that were torn and sewn up,
verses.9:5: and very old sandals that had been sewn with patches as a sign of age, clothed in old garments; the loaves also, which they carried for travel provisions, were hard and crumbled into pieces:
verses.9:6: and they went to Joshua, who was then staying in the camp of Gilgal, and said to him, and at the same time to all Israel, "We have come from a distant land, desiring to make peace with you." And the men of Israel answered them and said:
verses.9:7: "Perhaps you live in the land that is owed to us by lot, and we cannot enter into a covenant with you."
verses.9:8: But they said to Joshua, "We are your servants." Joshua said to them, "Who are you? And where have you come from?"
verses.9:9: They answered, "From a very distant land your servants have come in the name of the Lord your God. For we have heard the report of His power, everything that He did in Egypt,
verses.9:10: and to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, Sihon king of Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who was in Ashtaroth:
verses.9:11: and the elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us, 'Take provisions in your hands for the very long journey, and go to meet them, and say, "We are your servants; enter into a covenant with us."'
verses.9:12: Look at these loaves: we took them warm when we went out from our houses to come to you; now they have become dry and crumbled from excessive age.
verses.9:13: We filled new wineskins; now they have burst and come apart. The garments and sandals in which we are clothed and which we have on our feet are worn out and almost consumed because of the length of the very long journey."
verses.9:14: Therefore they took some of their provisions, and did not inquire of the mouth of the Lord.
verses.9:15: And Joshua made peace with them, and having entered into a covenant, he promised that they would not be killed; the leaders of the multitude also swore to them.
verses.9:16: Now three days after the covenant had been entered into, they heard that they lived nearby and would be among them.
verses.9:17: And the sons of Israel moved camp and came to their cities on the third day, whose names are these: Gibeon, and Chephirah, and Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
verses.9:18: And they did not strike them, because the leaders of the multitude had sworn to them in the name of the Lord God of Israel. Therefore the entire populace grumbled against the leaders.
verses.9:19: They answered them, "We have sworn to them in the name of the Lord God of Israel, and for that reason we cannot touch them.
verses.9:20: But this we will do to them: let them indeed be spared to live, so that the wrath of the Lord may not be stirred up against us if we perjure ourselves;
verses.9:21: rather, let them live in this way, so that they cut wood and carry water for the use of the whole multitude." While they were saying these things,
verses.9:22: Joshua called the Gibeonites and said to them, "Why did you want to deceive us by fraud, so as to say, 'We live very far from you,' when you are in our midst?
verses.9:23: Therefore you will be under a curse, and from your lineage there will not fail one cutting wood and carrying water into the house of my God."
verses.9:24: They answered, "It was reported to us, your servants, that the Lord your God had promised Moses His servant that He would hand over to you the entire land and destroy all its inhabitants. Therefore we were greatly afraid, and we provided for our lives, compelled by terror of you, and we entered into this plan.
verses.9:25: Now, however, we are in your hand: what seems good and right to you, do to us."
verses.9:26: So Joshua did as he had said, and rescued them from the hand of the sons of Israel, so that they would not be killed.
verses.9:27: And he decreed on that day that they should be in the service of all the people and of the altar of the Lord, cutting wood and carrying water, until the present time, in the place that the Lord would choose.
verses.10:1: When Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem had heard these things, namely, that Joshua had captured Ai and overthrown it (for just as he had done to Jericho and its king, so he did to Ai and its king), and that the Gibeonites had defected to Israel and were their allies,
verses.10:2: he feared greatly. For Gibeon was a great city, and one of the royal cities, and larger than the town of Ai, and all its warriors were very mighty.
verses.10:3: Therefore Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, and to Piram king of Jarmuth, also to Japhia king of Lachish, and to Debir king of Eglon, saying:
verses.10:4: "Come up to me and bring aid, so that we may conquer Gibeon, because it has defected to Joshua and to the sons of Israel."
verses.10:5: Therefore the five kings of the Amorites gathered and went up: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon, together with their armies; and they encamped around Gibeon, attacking it.
verses.10:6: Now the inhabitants of Gibeon, the besieged city, sent to Joshua, who was then staying in the camp at Gilgal, and said to him, "Do not withdraw your hands from helping your servants; come up quickly and rescue us, and bring aid, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have come together against us."
verses.10:7: And Joshua went up from Gilgal, and the whole army of warriors with him, very mighty men.
verses.10:8: And the Lord said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for I have handed them over into your hands; none of them will be able to resist you."
verses.10:9: Therefore Joshua rushed upon them suddenly, going up all night from Gilgal.
verses.10:10: And the Lord threw them into confusion before the face of Israel, and crushed them with a great slaughter in Gibeon, and pursued them along the road of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.
verses.10:11: And as they were fleeing from the sons of Israel and were on the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord cast large stones upon them from heaven as far as Azekah; and many more died from the hailstones than those whom the sons of Israel had struck with the sword.
verses.10:12: Then Joshua spoke to the Lord on the day when He handed over the Amorite in the sight of the sons of Israel, and he said before them, "Sun, do not move opposite Gibeon, and moon, opposite the valley of Aijalon."
verses.10:13: And the sun and the moon stood still until the nation avenged itself on its enemies. Is this not written in the book of the just? Therefore the sun stood still in the middle of heaven, and did not hasten to set for the space of one day.
verses.10:14: There was not before nor afterward so long a day, with the Lord obeying the voice of a man and fighting for Israel.
verses.10:15: And Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
verses.10:16: For the five kings had fled and had hidden themselves in the cave of the city of Makkedah.
verses.10:17: And it was reported to Joshua that the five kings had been found hiding in the cave of the city of Makkedah.
verses.10:18: He commanded his companions and said, "Roll huge stones to the mouth of the cave, and station diligent men to guard them shut inside;
verses.10:19: as for you, do not stand still, but pursue the enemies, and cut down all the rearmost of those fleeing; and do not allow them to enter the strongholds of their cities, whom the Lord God has handed over into your hands."
verses.10:20: Therefore, when the adversaries had been cut down with a great slaughter and almost consumed to utter destruction, those who were able to escape Israel entered the fortified cities.
verses.10:21: And the entire army returned to Joshua at Makkedah, where the camp then was, unharmed and in full number; and no one dared to mutter against the sons of Israel.
verses.10:22: And Joshua commanded, saying, "Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out to me the five kings who are hiding in it."
verses.10:23: And the attendants did as had been ordered them, and led out to him the five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon.
verses.10:24: And when they had been led out to him, he called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the army who were with him, "Go and put your feet on the necks of these kings." When they had gone forward and were treading with their feet on the necks of those subdued,
verses.10:25: he said to them again, "Do not fear, nor be terrified; be strengthened and be resolute, for thus the Lord will do to all your enemies against whom you fight."
verses.10:26: And Joshua struck them and killed them, and hanged them on five stakes; and they were hanging until evening.
verses.10:27: And when the sun was setting, he commanded his companions to take them down from the gibbets. Having taken them down, they threw them into the cave in which they had hidden, and placed huge stones over its mouth, which remain until the present.
verses.10:28: On that same day also, Joshua captured Makkedah and struck it with the edge of the sword, and killed its king and all its inhabitants; he did not leave in it even a small remnant. And he did to the king of Makkedah just as he had done to the king of Jericho.
verses.10:29: Then he passed with all Israel from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against it:
verses.10:30: which the Lord handed over, along with its king, into the hands of Israel; and they struck the city with the edge of the sword, and all its inhabitants; they did not leave in it any remnant. And they did to the king of Libnah just as they had done to the king of Jericho.
verses.10:31: From Libnah he passed to Lachish with all Israel, and having deployed the army all around, he attacked it.
verses.10:32: And the Lord handed over Lachish into the hands of Israel, and he captured it on the second day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every soul that had been in it, just as he had done to Libnah.
verses.10:33: At that time Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish; and Joshua struck him with all his people to utter destruction.
verses.10:34: And he passed from Lachish to Eglon and surrounded it,
verses.10:35: and conquered it on the same day; and he struck with the edge of the sword all the souls that were in it, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
verses.10:36: He also went up with all Israel from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it:
verses.10:37: he captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, its king also, and all the towns of that region, and all the souls that had lived in it; he did not leave in it any remnant; just as he had done to Eglon, so he did also to Hebron, consuming with the sword everything that he found in it.
verses.10:38: Turning back from there to Debir,
verses.10:39: he captured it and laid it waste; its king also, and all the surrounding towns, he struck with the edge of the sword; he did not leave in it any remnant; just as he had done to Hebron and Libnah and their kings, so he did to Debir and its king.
verses.10:40: Therefore Joshua struck all the hill country and the south and the plains, and Ashdoth, with their kings; he did not leave in it any remnant, but he killed everything that could breathe, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded him,
verses.10:41: from Kadesh-barnea as far as Gaza. All the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon,
verses.10:42: and all the kings and their regions he captured and laid waste in one assault, for the Lord God of Israel fought for him.
verses.10:43: And he returned with all Israel to the site of the camp in Gilgal.
verses.11:1: When Jabin, king of Hazor, had heard these things, he sent to Jobab, king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
verses.11:2: and also to the kings of the north, who lived in the hill country and in the plain south of Chinneroth, in the lowlands also and in the regions of Dor beside the sea,
verses.11:3: and also to the Canaanite on the east and the west, and the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, and the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite also, who lived at the foot of Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
verses.11:4: And they all went out with their troops, an exceedingly numerous people, like the sand that is on the shore of the sea, and horses and chariots also, in an immense multitude.
verses.11:5: And all these kings came together as one at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
verses.11:6: And the Lord said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for tomorrow at this same hour I will deliver all of these to be wounded in the sight of Israel; you shall hamstring their horses and burn the chariots with fire."
verses.11:7: And Joshua, and the whole army with him, came suddenly against them at the waters of Merom, and they rushed upon them,
verses.11:8: and the Lord delivered them into the hands of Israel. And they struck them down and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, and the waters of Misrephoth, and the plain of Mizpah, which is on its eastern side. He struck all of them down so that he left no remnant of them.
verses.11:9: And he did just as the Lord had commanded him: he hamstrung their horses and burned the chariots with fire.
verses.11:10: And turning back at once, he captured Hazor and struck down its king with the sword. For in former times Hazor held the primacy among all these kingdoms.
verses.11:11: And he struck down all the souls who lived there; he left no remnant in it, but devastated everything to utter destruction, and destroyed the city itself by fire.
verses.11:12: And he captured, struck down, and destroyed all the surrounding cities and their kings, just as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded him.
verses.11:13: Apart from the cities that were situated on hills and on mounds, Israel burned the rest; flame consumed one alone, Hazor, the most strongly fortified.
verses.11:14: And the sons of Israel divided for themselves all the plunder of these cities and the livestock, after all the people had been killed.
verses.11:15: Just as the Lord had commanded Moses His servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and he fulfilled everything; he did not omit, from all the commands, even a single word that the Lord had ordered Moses.
verses.11:16: So Joshua captured all the hill country and the southern land, and the land of Goshen, and the plain, and the western region, and the mountain of Israel and its lowlands,
verses.11:17: and the part of the mountain that ascends to Seir, as far as Baal-gad, through the plain of Lebanon beneath Mount Hermon; all their kings he captured, struck down, and put to death.
verses.11:18: For a long time Joshua fought against these kings.
verses.11:19: There was not a city that surrendered itself to the sons of Israel, except the Hivite who lived in Gibeon; for he captured them all by waging war.
verses.11:20: For it had been the decree of the Lord that their hearts should be hardened, and that they should fight against Israel, and fall, and not deserve any mercy, and perish, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.11:21: At that time Joshua came and killed the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and from all the mountain of Judah and Israel, and destroyed their cities.
verses.11:22: He left no one of the lineage of the Anakim in the land of the sons of Israel, apart from the cities of Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod, in which alone they were left.
verses.11:23: Therefore Joshua captured the whole land, just as the Lord spoke to Moses, and gave it as a possession to the sons of Israel according to their portions and tribes; and the land rested from battles.
verses.12:1: These are the kings whom the sons of Israel struck down, and whose land they possessed beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the stream of Arnon as far as Mount Hermon, and all the eastern region that faces the wilderness.
verses.12:2: Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, ruled from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the stream of Arnon, and over the middle part in the valley, and over half of Gilead, as far as the stream of Jabbok, which is the border of the sons of Ammon;
verses.12:3: and from the wilderness as far as the Sea of Chinneroth toward the east, and as far as the sea of the desert, which is the Saltiest Sea, toward the eastern region by the road that leads to Beth-jeshimoth, and on the southern side, which lies beneath Ashdoth, Pisgah.
verses.12:4: The territory of Og, king of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived in Ashtaroth and in Edrei, and ruled in Mount Hermon, and in Salecah, and in all Bashan, as far as the borders
verses.12:5: of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and of half of Gilead, the borders of Sihon, king of Heshbon.
verses.12:6: Moses the servant of the Lord and the sons of Israel struck them down, and Moses gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.12:7: These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the sons of Israel struck down beyond the Jordan toward the western region, from Baal-gad in the plain of Lebanon as far as the mountain a part of which ascends into Seir; and Joshua gave it as a possession to the tribes of Israel, to each their portions,
verses.12:8: both in the hill country and in the plains and the lowlands. In Ashdoth, and in the wilderness, and in the south, were the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite.
verses.12:9: The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
verses.12:10: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
verses.12:11: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
verses.12:12: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
verses.12:13: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
verses.12:14: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
verses.12:15: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
verses.12:16: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
verses.12:17: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
verses.12:18: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Sharon, one;
verses.12:19: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
verses.12:20: the king of Shimron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
verses.12:21: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
verses.12:22: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jachanan of Carmel, one;
verses.12:23: the king of Dor and of the province of Dor, one; the king of the nations of Gilgal, one;
verses.12:24: the king of Tirzah, one: thirty-one kings in all.
verses.13:1: Joshua was old and advanced in age, and the Lord said to him, "You have grown old and are of great age, and a very extensive land has been left, which has not yet been divided by lot:
verses.13:2: namely, all Galilee of the Philistines, and all Geshur.
verses.13:3: From the muddy river that waters Egypt as far as the borders of Ekron toward the north, the land of Canaan, which is divided among the five rulers of the Philistines: the Gazites, the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites.
verses.13:4: To the south, moreover, are the Hivites, all the land of Canaan, and Mearah of the Sidonians, as far as Aphek and the borders of the Amorites,
verses.13:5: and its borderlands. Also the region of Lebanon toward the east, from Baal-gad beneath Mount Hermon until you enter Hamath;
verses.13:6: of all who dwell in the hill country from Lebanon as far as the waters of Misrephoth, and all the Sidonians. It is I who will wipe them out from before the sons of Israel. Therefore let it come into the portion of the inheritance of Israel, just as I commanded you.
verses.13:7: And now divide the land as a possession for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
verses.13:8: With it, Reuben and Gad possessed the land that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave to them across the streams of the Jordan, toward the eastern region:
verses.13:9: from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the stream of Arnon and in the middle of the valley, and all the plains of Medeba as far as Dibon,
verses.13:10: and all the cities of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the borders of the sons of Ammon,
verses.13:11: and Gilead, and the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah,
verses.13:12: all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei; he himself was of the remnant of the Rephaim, and Moses struck them down and wiped them out.
verses.13:13: Yet the sons of Israel were unwilling to destroy the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and they have lived in the midst of Israel to the present day.
verses.13:14: To the tribe of Levi, however, he did not give a possession; rather, the sacrifices and offerings of the Lord God of Israel are themselves its inheritance, just as He spoke to it.
verses.13:15: Therefore Moses gave a possession to the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their clans.
verses.13:16: And their territory was from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the stream of Arnon and in the middle of the valley of that same stream: all the plain that leads to Medeba,
verses.13:17: and Heshbon, and all their small villages that are in the plains; also Dibon and Bamoth-baal, and the town of Baal-meon,
verses.13:18: and Jahaz, and Kedemoth, and Mephaath,
verses.13:19: and Kiriathaim, and Sibmah, and Zereth-shahar on the mountain of the valley;
verses.13:20: Beth-peor and Ashdoth, Pisgah and Beth-jeshimoth,
verses.13:21: and all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdoms of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck down along with the princes of Midian: Heveus, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, leaders of Sihon, inhabitants of the land.
verses.13:22: And the sons of Israel killed Balaam the son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword, along with the others who were put to death.
verses.13:23: And the border of the sons of Reuben became the Jordan River. This is the possession of the Reubenites by their clans: cities and small villages.
verses.13:24: And Moses gave a possession to the tribe of Gad and to his sons by their clans, of which this is the division:
verses.13:25: the territory of Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half of the land of the sons of Ammon, as far as Aroer, which is opposite Rabbah,
verses.13:26: and from Heshbon as far as Ramoth, Mizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim as far as the borders of Debir.
verses.13:27: Also in the valley: Beth-haram, and Beth-nimrah, and Succoth, and Zaphon, the remaining part of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon; its boundary also is the Jordan, as far as the farthest part of the Sea of Chinnereth across the Jordan, toward the eastern region.
verses.13:28: This is the possession of the sons of Gad by their families: the cities and their villages.
verses.13:29: He also gave a possession to the half-tribe of Manasseh and to his sons according to their clans,
verses.13:30: of which this is the beginning: from Mahanaim, all Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Og, king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty towns;
verses.13:31: and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, for the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, for half of the sons of Machir according to their clans.
verses.13:32: Moses divided this possession in the plains of Moab across the Jordan, opposite Jericho, toward the eastern region.
verses.13:33: To the tribe of Levi, however, he did not give a possession, because the Lord God of Israel Himself is its possession, just as He spoke to it.
verses.14:1: This is what the sons of Israel possessed in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the leaders of the families throughout the tribes of Israel gave to them,
verses.14:2: dividing everything by lot, just as the Lord had commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
verses.14:3: For to the two tribes and a half Moses had given a possession across the Jordan, apart from the Levites, who received no land among their brothers;
verses.14:4: but the sons of Joseph, divided into two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, succeeded to their place; nor did the Levites receive any other portion in the land except cities to live in, and their surrounding lands for feeding their beasts of burden and their livestock.
verses.14:5: Just as the Lord had commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did, and they divided the land.
verses.14:6: Therefore the sons of Judah approached Joshua in Gilgal, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the Kenizzite, spoke to him, "You know what the Lord spoke to Moses, the man of God, concerning me and you in Kadesh-barnea.
verses.14:7: I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of the Lord, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to examine the land, and I reported to him what seemed true to me.
verses.14:8: My brothers, however, who had gone up with me, melted the heart of the people; and nevertheless I followed the Lord my God.
verses.14:9: And Moses swore on that day, saying, 'The land that your foot stepped on will be your possession and that of your sons forever, because you have followed the Lord my God.'
verses.14:10: Therefore the Lord has granted me life, just as He promised, to the present day. It has been forty-five years since the Lord spoke this word to Moses, while Israel was walking through the wilderness; today I am eighty-five years old,
verses.14:11: just as strong as I was at that time when I was sent to explore; the strength of that time endures in me to this day, both for waging war and for marching.
verses.14:12: Therefore give me this hill country that the Lord promised while you also were listening, in which the Anakim are, and great and fortified cities, if perhaps the Lord will be with me and I will be able to wipe them out, just as He promised me."
verses.14:13: And Joshua blessed him, and gave him Hebron as a possession;
verses.14:14: and from then on Hebron belonged to Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the Kenizzite, to the present day, because he followed the Lord God of Israel.
verses.14:15: The name of Hebron was previously called Kiriath-arba; Adam, the greatest among the Anakim, lies buried there; and the land ceased from battles.
verses.15:1: Therefore the lot of the sons of Judah by their clans was this: from the border of Edom, the wilderness of Zin, toward the south, and as far as the farthest part of the southern region.
verses.15:2: Its beginning is from the end of the Saltiest Sea, and from its tongue that faces the south.
verses.15:3: And it goes out toward the ascent of the Scorpion, and passes on to Zin; and it goes up to Kadesh-barnea, and reaches Hezron, going up to Addar, and curving around Karka,
verses.15:4: and from there passing on to Azmon, and reaching the stream of Egypt; and its borders will be the Great Sea. This will be the boundary of the southern region.
verses.15:5: Now on the east the beginning will be the Saltiest Sea as far as the farthest end of the Jordan; and the parts that face toward the north are from the tongue of the sea as far as that same Jordan River.
verses.15:6: And the border goes up to Beth-hoglah, and passes on the north to Beth-arabah, going up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben,
verses.15:7: and stretching as far as the borders of Debir from the valley of Achor, toward the north facing Gilgal, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, on the southern side of the stream; and it crosses the waters that are called the Spring of the Sun; and its outlets will be at the spring of Rogel.
verses.15:8: And it goes up through the valley of the son of Hinnom on the side of the Jebusite toward the south, that is, Jerusalem; and rising from there to the top of the mountain that is opposite Gehennom toward the west, at the end of the valley of Rephaim toward the north,
verses.15:9: and it passes on from the top of the mountain as far as the spring of the water of Nephtoah; and it reaches as far as the towns of Mount Ephron; and it turns toward Baalah, which is Kiriath-jearim, that is, the city of forests.
verses.15:10: And it curves around from Baalah toward the west, as far as Mount Seir; and it passes along the side of Mount Jearim toward the north to Chesalon; and it goes down to Beth-shemesh, and passes to Timnah.
verses.15:11: And it reaches toward the north of the region of Ekron on the side; and it turns to Shikkeron, and crosses Mount Baalah; and it reaches Jabneel, and ends at the boundary of the Great Sea toward the west.
verses.15:12: These are the borders of the sons of Judah all around in their clans.
verses.15:13: Now to Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a portion in the midst of the sons of Judah, just as the Lord had commanded him: Kiriath-arba of the father of Anak, which is Hebron.
verses.15:14: And from it Caleb wiped out the three sons of Anak, Sheshai and Ahiman and Talmai, of the lineage of Anak.
verses.15:15: And going up from there, he came to the inhabitants of Debir, which previously was called Kiriath-sepher, that is, the city of letters.
verses.15:16: And Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, to him I will give my daughter Achsah as a wife."
verses.15:17: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb, captured it; and he gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
verses.15:18: And as they were going along together, she was persuaded by her husband to ask her father for a field. And she sighed as she sat on the donkey; and Caleb said to her, "What is the matter with you?"
verses.15:19: And she answered, "Give me a blessing: you have given me a southern and dry land; add also watered land." So Caleb gave her the upper and lower watered land.
verses.15:20: This is the possession of the tribe of the sons of Judah by their clans.
verses.15:21: And the cities from the farthest parts of the sons of Judah next to the borders of Edom on the south were: Kabzeel and Eder and Jagur,
verses.15:22: and Kinah and Dimonah and Adadah,
verses.15:23: and Kedesh and Hazor and Ithnan,
verses.15:25: New Hazor and Kerioth, Hezron, that is, Hazor;
verses.15:27: and Hazar-gaddah and Heshmon and Beth-pelet,
verses.15:28: and Hazar-shual and Beersheba and Biziothiah,
verses.15:29: and Baalah and Iim and Ezem,
verses.15:30: and Eltolad and Chesil and Hormah,
verses.15:31: and Ziklag and Madmannah and Sansannah,
verses.15:32: Lebaoth and Shilhim and Ain and Rimmon. All the cities were twenty-nine, and their villages.
verses.15:33: Now in the plains: Eshtaol and Zorah and Ashnah,
verses.15:34: and Zanoah and En-gannim and Tappuah and Enam,
verses.15:35: and Jarmuth and Adullam, Socoh and Azekah,
verses.15:36: and Shaaraim and Adithaim and Gederah and Gederothaim: fourteen cities, and their villages.
verses.15:41: and Gederoth and Beth-dagon and Naamah and Makkedah: sixteen cities, and their villages.
verses.15:44: and Keilah and Achzib and Mareshah: nine cities, and their villages.
verses.15:45: Ekron, with its towns and small villages.
verses.15:46: From Ekron as far as the sea: all that lies toward Ashdod and its small towns.
verses.15:47: Ashdod, with its towns and small villages. Gaza, with its towns and small villages, as far as the stream of Egypt, and the Great Sea is its border.
verses.15:48: And in the hill country: Shamir and Jattir and Socoh,
verses.15:49: and Dannah and Kiriath-sannah, that is, Debir;
verses.15:51: Goshen and Holon and Giloh: eleven cities and their villages.
verses.15:53: and Janum and Beth-tappuah and Aphekah,
verses.15:54: Humtah, and Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, and Zior: nine cities, and their villages.
verses.15:55: Maon and Carmel and Ziph and Juttah,
verses.15:57: Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah: ten cities and their villages.
verses.15:59: Maarath, and Beth-anoth, and Eltekon: six cities and their villages.
verses.15:60: Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, the city of forests, and Rabbah: two cities, and their villages.
verses.15:61: In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, and Secacah,
verses.15:62: and Nibshan, and the City of Salt, and En-gedi: six cities, and their villages.
verses.15:63: But the sons of Judah could not wipe out the Jebusite, the inhabitant of Jerusalem; and the Jebusite lived with the sons of Judah in Jerusalem up to the present day.
verses.16:1: The lot of the sons of Joseph also fell from the Jordan opposite Jericho and its waters on the east: the wilderness that goes up from Jericho to the mountain of Bethel,
verses.16:2: and it goes out from Bethel, Luz, and crosses the border of Archi, Ataroth,
verses.16:3: and goes down to the west along the border of Japhleti, as far as the borders of Lower Beth-horon and Gezer; and its regions end at the Great Sea.
verses.16:4: And the sons of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took possession.
verses.16:5: And the border of the sons of Ephraim by their clans, and their possession toward the east, was Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon.
verses.16:6: And the borders go out to the sea; now Michmethath faces the north, and it goes around the borders toward the east to Taanath-shiloh, and passes along on the east of Janoah.
verses.16:7: And it goes down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, and reaches Jericho, and goes out to the Jordan.
verses.16:8: From Tappuah it passes along toward the sea to the valley of the reed bed, and its extremities are at the Saltiest Sea. This is the possession of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim by their families.
verses.16:9: And cities were set apart for the sons of Ephraim in the midst of the possession of the sons of Manasseh, and their villages.
verses.16:10: And the sons of Ephraim did not kill the Canaanite who lived in Gezer, and the Canaanite lived in the midst of Ephraim until this day as a tributary.
verses.17:1: Now the lot fell to the tribe of Manasseh (for he is the firstborn of Joseph): to Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, who was a warrior and had the possession of Gilead and Bashan,
verses.17:2: and to the rest of the sons of Manasseh according to their families: to the sons of Abiezer, and to the sons of Helek, and to the sons of Asriel, and to the sons of Shechem, and to the sons of Hepher, and to the sons of Shemida. These are the sons of Manasseh, the son of Joseph, the males, by their clans.
verses.17:3: Now Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but only daughters, whose names are these: Mahlah, and Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
verses.17:4: And they came into the presence of Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the leaders, saying, "The Lord commanded through the hand of Moses that a possession be given to us in the midst of our brothers." And he gave them, according to the command of the Lord, a possession in the midst of their father's brothers.
verses.17:5: And ten measuring lines fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan across the Jordan.
verses.17:6: For the daughters of Manasseh possessed an inheritance in the midst of his sons. And the land of Gilead fell to the lot of the sons of Manasseh who remained.
verses.17:7: And the border of Manasseh was from Asher, Michmethath, which faces Shechem; and it goes out to the right beside the inhabitants of the spring of Tappuah.
verses.17:8: For the land of Tappuah had fallen in the lot of Manasseh, which, beside the borders of Manasseh, belongs to the sons of Ephraim.
verses.17:9: And the border of the valley of the reed bed goes down to the south of the stream of the cities of Ephraim, which are in the midst of the cities of Manasseh; the border of Manasseh is on the north of the stream, and its extremity goes to the sea,
verses.17:10: so that the possession of Ephraim is on the south, and on the north that of Manasseh, and the sea encloses both, and they are joined to one another in the tribe of Asher on the north, and in the tribe of Issachar on the east.
verses.17:11: And the inheritance of Manasseh in Issachar and in Asher was Beth-shean and its villages, and Ibleam with its villages, and the inhabitants of Dor with its towns, the inhabitants of En-dor also with its villages, and likewise the inhabitants of Taanach with its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo with its villages, and a third part of the city of Naphoth.
verses.17:12: And the sons of Manasseh could not overthrow these cities, but the Canaanite began to live in his land.
verses.17:13: Now after the sons of Israel grew strong, they subdued the Canaanites and made them tributaries to themselves, and did not kill them.
verses.17:14: And the sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua and said, "Why have you given me the possession of one lot and measuring line, since I am so great a multitude, and the Lord has blessed me?"
verses.17:15: To them Joshua said, "If you are a numerous people, go up into the forest and cut out spaces for yourself in the land of the Perizzite and of the Rephaim, because the possession of Mount Ephraim is too narrow for you."
verses.17:16: The sons of Joseph answered him, "We will not be able to go up to the hill country, since the Canaanites use iron chariots, those who live in the level land in which are situated Beth-shean with its villages, and Jezreel, possessing the middle of the valley."
verses.17:17: And Joshua said to the house of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a numerous people, and of great strength; you will not have one lot,
verses.17:18: but you will pass over to the mountain, and you will cut down for yourself and clear spaces to live in; and you will be able to proceed further when you have overthrown the Canaanite, who, you say, has iron chariots and is very strong."
verses.18:1: And all the sons of Israel were assembled at Shiloh, and there they set up the tabernacle of the testimony, and the land was subject to them.
verses.18:2: Now there had remained seven tribes of the sons of Israel that had not yet received their possessions.
verses.18:3: To them Joshua said, "How long will you languish in idleness and not enter to possess the land that the Lord God of your fathers has given you?
verses.18:4: Choose three men from each tribe, so that I may send them, and they may set out and go around the land, and describe it according to the number of each one's multitude, and bring back to me what they have described.
verses.18:5: Divide the land for yourselves into seven parts: let Judah be in its borders on the southern side, and the house of Joseph on the north.
verses.18:6: Describe the middle land between these in seven parts, and you will come here to me, so that I may cast the lot for you here before the Lord your God,
verses.18:7: because there is no portion for the Levites among you, but the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. And Gad and Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, had already received their possessions across the Jordan on the eastern side, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave them."
verses.18:8: And when the men had risen to set out to describe the land, Joshua commanded them, saying, "Go around the land and describe it, and return to me, so that here before the Lord, at Shiloh, I may cast the lot for you."
verses.18:9: Therefore they set out, and surveying it, they divided it into seven parts, writing in a scroll. And they returned to Joshua at the camp of Shiloh.
verses.18:10: And he cast lots before the Lord at Shiloh, and divided the land for the sons of Israel into seven parts.
verses.18:11: And the first lot of the sons of Benjamin came up by their families, so that they would possess the land between the sons of Judah and the sons of Joseph.
verses.18:12: And their border on the north was from the Jordan, proceeding along the flank of Jericho on the northern side, and from there going up toward the west to the hill country, and reaching the wilderness of Beth-aven,
verses.18:13: and passing along beside Luz to the south, that is, Bethel; and it goes down to Ataroth-addar, to the mountain that is to the south of Lower Beth-horon,
verses.18:14: and it bends, going around toward the sea to the south of the mountain that faces Beth-horon toward the southwest; and its extremities are at Kiriath-baal, which is also called Kiriath-jearim, a city of the sons of Judah. This is the side toward the sea, to the west.
verses.18:15: Now on the south, from the side of Kiriath-jearim, the border goes out toward the sea, and reaches as far as the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.
verses.18:16: And it goes down to the part of the mountain that faces the valley of the sons of Hinnom, and it is toward the northern side at the farthest part of the valley of Rephaim. And it goes down to Gehennom (that is, the valley of Hinnom) along the flank of the Jebusite to the south, and reaches the spring of Rogel,
verses.18:17: passing over to the north, and going out to En-shemesh, that is, the spring of the sun,
verses.18:18: and it passes along as far as the mounds that are opposite the ascent of Adummim; and it goes down to Eben-bohan, that is, the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben; and it passes along on the northern flank to the plains, and goes down into the plain,
verses.18:19: and passes by on the north of Beth-hoglah; and its extremities are opposite the tongue of the Saltiest Sea on the north, at the end of the Jordan on the southern side,
verses.18:20: which is its border on the east. This is the possession of the sons of Benjamin by their borders all around, and their families.
verses.18:21: And its cities were Jericho, and Beth-hoglah, and the valley of Keziz,
verses.18:23: and Avvim, and Parah, and Ophrah,
verses.18:24: the village of Ammonah, and Ophni, and Geba: twelve cities, and their villages.
verses.18:26: and Mizpeh, and Chephirah, and Mozah,
verses.18:28: and Zela, Eleph, and Jebus, which is Jerusalem, Gibeath, and Kiriath: fourteen cities, and their villages. This is the possession of the sons of Benjamin according to their families.
verses.19:1: And the second lot of the sons of Simeon came out by their clans, and their inheritance was
verses.19:2: in the midst of the possession of the sons of Judah: Beersheba, and Sheba, and Moladah,
verses.19:5: and Ziklag, and Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah,
verses.19:6: and Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen: thirteen cities and their villages.
verses.19:7: Ain, and Rimmon, and Ether, and Ashan: four cities and their villages;
verses.19:8: all the hamlets around these cities as far as Baalath-beer, Ramath, toward the southern region. This is the inheritance of the sons of Simeon according to their clans,
verses.19:9: in the possession and measuring line of the sons of Judah, because it was too large; and therefore the sons of Simeon took possession in the midst of their inheritance.
verses.19:10: And the third lot of the sons of Zebulun fell by their clans; the border of their possession extended as far as Sarid.
verses.19:11: And it goes up from the sea and Maralah, and reaches to Dabbesheth, as far as the brook that is opposite Jokneam.
verses.19:12: And it turns back from Sarid toward the east to the borders of Chisloth-tabor, and goes out to Daberath, and goes up toward Japhia.
verses.19:13: And from there it passes over as far as the eastern side of Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, and goes out to Rimmon, Amthar, and Neah.
verses.19:14: And it circles Hannathon to the north, and its endpoints are the valley of Iphtah-el,
verses.19:15: and Kattath, and Nahalal, and Shimron, and Jerala, and Bethlehem: twelve cities and their villages.
verses.19:16: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun by their clans, the cities and their hamlets.
verses.19:17: For Issachar the fourth lot came out by its clans,
verses.19:18: and its inheritance was Jezreel, and Chesulloth, and Shunem,
verses.19:19: and Hapharaim, and Shion, and Anaharath,
verses.19:21: and Remeth, and En-gannim, and En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez.
verses.19:22: And its border reached as far as Tabor, and Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, and its endpoints will be the Jordan: sixteen cities and their villages.
verses.19:23: This is the possession of the sons of Issachar by their clans, the cities and their hamlets.
verses.19:24: And the fifth lot fell to the tribe of the sons of Asher by their clans,
verses.19:25: and their border was Helkath, and Hali, and Beten, and Achshaph,
verses.19:26: and Allammelech, and Amad, and Mishal; and it reaches as far as Carmel of the sea, and Shihor and Libnath,
verses.19:27: and turns back toward the east to Beth-dagon, and passes over to Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el toward the north, to Beth-emek and Neiel. And it goes out to the left, to Cabul,
verses.19:28: and Ebron, and Rehob, and Hammon, and Kanah, as far as great Sidon.
verses.19:29: And it turns back to Hormah as far as the strongly fortified city of Tyre, and as far as Hosah; and its endpoints will be at the sea from the measuring line of Achzib,
verses.19:30: and Ummah, and Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two cities and their villages.
verses.19:31: This is the possession of the sons of Asher by their clans, both the cities and their hamlets.
verses.19:32: The sixth lot of the sons of Naphtali fell by their families,
verses.19:33: and the border began from Heleph and Elon in Zaanannim, and Adami, which is Nekeb, and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum; and their endpoints were as far as the Jordan;
verses.19:34: and the border turns back toward the west to Aznoth-tabor, and from there goes out to Hukkok, and passes over to Zebulun toward the south, and to Asher toward the west, and to Judah at the Jordan toward the rising of the sun;
verses.19:35: the strongly fortified cities: Ziddim, Zer, and Hammath, and Rakkath, and Chinnereth,
verses.19:38: and Iron, and Migdal-el, Horem, and Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh: nineteen cities and their villages.
verses.19:39: This is the possession of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali by their clans, the cities and their hamlets.
verses.19:40: For the tribe of the sons of Dan by their families, the seventh lot came out,
verses.19:41: and the border of its possession was Zorah, and Eshtaol, and Ir-shemesh, that is, the city of the sun.
