verses.19:45: and Jehud, and Bene, and Berak, and Gath-rimmon,
verses.19:46: and Me-jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border that faces Joppa.
verses.19:47: And it is bounded by that very border. And the sons of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, and captured it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and took possession and lived in it, calling its name Leshem Dan, after the name of Dan their father.
verses.19:48: This is the possession of the tribe of the sons of Dan by their clans, the cities and their hamlets.
verses.19:49: And when he had finished dividing the land by lot to each one by their tribes, the sons of Israel gave a possession to Joshua the son of Nun in their midst,
verses.19:50: according to the command of the Lord, the city that he requested, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city and lived in it.
verses.19:51: These are the possessions that Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the leaders of the families and tribes of the sons of Israel divided by lot in Shiloh, before the Lord at the entrance of the tabernacle of the testimony; and they apportioned the land.
verses.20:1: And the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying, "Speak to the sons of Israel, and say to them,
verses.20:2: 'Set apart the cities of fugitives, about which I spoke to you through the hand of Moses,
verses.20:3: so that whoever has struck a person unknowingly may flee to them, and may be able to escape the wrath of the kinsman who is the avenger of blood.
verses.20:4: When he flees to one of these cities, he will stand in front of the city gate and tell the elders of that city the things that prove him innocent; and so they will take him in and give him a place to live.
verses.20:5: And when the avenger of blood pursues him, they will not surrender him into his hands, because he struck his neighbor unknowingly and is not shown to have been his enemy two or three days earlier.
verses.20:6: And he will live in that city until he stands before the court, rendering an account of his deed, and until the high priest who is in office at that time dies; then the killer will return and enter his city and his house, from which he had fled.'"
verses.20:7: And they designated Kedesh in Galilee of the hill country of Naphtali, and Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.
verses.20:8: And beyond the Jordan toward the eastern side of Jericho, they appointed Bezer, which is situated in the wilderness plain, from the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.
verses.20:9: These cities were established for all the sons of Israel, and for the foreigners who lived among them, so that the one who had struck a person unknowingly might flee to them, and might not die by the hand of the kinsman desiring to avenge the shed blood, until he stood before the people to present his case.
verses.21:1: And the heads of the families of Levi approached Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the leaders of the clans across each of the tribes of the sons of Israel.
verses.21:2: And they spoke to them in Shiloh of the land of Canaan and said, "The Lord commanded by the hand of Moses that cities be given to us to live in, and their outlying lands for feeding livestock."
verses.21:3: And the sons of Israel gave from their possessions, according to the command of the Lord, cities and their outlying lands.
verses.21:4: And the lot came out for the family of Kohath, of the sons of Aaron the priest: from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin, thirteen cities;
verses.21:5: and for the rest of the sons of Kohath, that is, the Levites who remained, from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, ten cities.
verses.21:6: Furthermore, as for the sons of Gershon, the lot came out that they should receive from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities in number.
verses.21:7: And for the sons of Merari by their clans, from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun, twelve cities.
verses.21:8: And the sons of Israel gave to the Levites cities and their outlying lands, just as the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses, assigning to each one by lot.
verses.21:9: From the tribes of the sons of Judah and Simeon, Joshua gave cities, whose names are these,
verses.21:10: to the sons of Aaron by the families of Kohath of Levitical descent (for the first lot came out for them):
verses.21:11: Kiriath-arba of the father of Anak, which is called Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, and its outlying lands all around.
verses.21:12: Its fields and its villages, however, he had given to Caleb the son of Jephunneh to possess.
verses.21:13: Therefore he gave to the sons of Aaron the priest Hebron, a city of refuge, and its outlying lands, and Libnah with its outlying lands,
verses.21:16: and Ain, and Juttah, and Beth-shemesh, with their outlying lands: nine cities from the two tribes, as has been said.
verses.21:17: And from the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, Gibeon and Geba,
verses.21:18: and Anathoth and Almon, with their outlying lands: four cities.
verses.21:19: All the cities together of the sons of Aaron the priest: thirteen, with their outlying lands.
verses.21:20: Now to the rest, by the families of the sons of Kohath of Levitical descent, this possession was given.
verses.21:21: From the tribe of Ephraim, cities of refuge: Shechem with its outlying lands in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer,
verses.21:22: and Kibzaim and Beth-horon, with their outlying lands, four cities.
verses.21:23: Also from the tribe of Dan, Elteke and Gibbethon,
verses.21:24: and Aijalon and Gath-rimmon, with their outlying lands, four cities.
verses.21:25: Furthermore, from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach and Gath-rimmon, with their outlying lands, two cities.
verses.21:26: All ten cities and their outlying lands were given to the sons of Kohath of the lower rank.
verses.21:27: Also to the sons of Gershon of Levitical descent he gave from the half-tribe of Manasseh cities of refuge: Golan in Bashan and Bosra, with their outlying lands, two cities.
verses.21:28: Furthermore, from the tribe of Issachar, Kishion and Daberath,
verses.21:29: and Jarmuth and En-gannim, with their outlying lands, four cities.
verses.21:30: And from the tribe of Asher, Mishal and Abdon,
verses.21:31: and Helkath and Rehob, with their outlying lands, four cities.
verses.21:32: Also from the tribe of Naphtali, cities of refuge: Kedesh in Galilee, and Hammoth-dor, and Kartan, with their outlying lands, three cities.
verses.21:33: All the cities of the families of Gershon: thirteen, with their outlying lands.
verses.21:34: Now to the sons of Merari, the Levites of the lower rank, by their families, from the tribe of Zebulun were given Jokneam and Kartah,
verses.21:35: and Dimnah and Nahalal, four cities with their outlying lands.
verses.21:36: From the tribe of Reuben beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho, cities of refuge: Bezer in the wilderness, Misor, and Jaser, and Jethson, and Mephaath, four cities with their outlying lands.
verses.21:37: From the tribe of Gad, cities of refuge: Ramoth in Gilead, and Mahanaim, and Heshbon, and Jazer, four cities with their outlying lands.
verses.21:38: All the cities of the sons of Merari by their families and clans: twelve.
verses.21:39: Thus all the cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the sons of Israel were forty-eight,
verses.21:40: with their outlying lands, each one distributed by families.
verses.21:41: And the Lord God gave to Israel all the land that He had sworn He would deliver to their fathers, and they took possession of it and lived in it.
verses.21:42: And peace was given by Him toward all the nations all around; and none of the enemies dared to resist them, but all were brought under their dominion.
verses.21:43: Not even one word that He had promised He would perform for them proved void, but all things were fulfilled in deeds.
verses.22:1: At that same time Joshua summoned the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh,
verses.22:2: and said to them, "You have done all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you; you have also obeyed me in all things,
verses.22:3: nor have you abandoned your brothers for a long time, until the present day, keeping the command of the Lord your God.
verses.22:4: Therefore, because the Lord your God has given your brothers rest and peace, just as He promised, return and go to your tents, and to the land of possession that Moses the servant of the Lord delivered to you across the Jordan,
verses.22:5: provided only that you carefully keep and fulfill in deed the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you: to love the Lord your God, and to walk in all His ways, and to observe His commandments, and to cling to Him and serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul."
verses.22:6: And Joshua blessed them and sent them away. And they returned to their tents.
verses.22:7: Now Moses had given a possession in Bashan to half the tribe of Manasseh, and therefore to the half that remained Joshua gave an allotment among their other brothers across the Jordan on the western side. And as he was sending them away to their tents and had blessed them,
verses.22:8: he said to them, "Return to your dwellings with much property and riches, with silver and gold, bronze and iron, and abundant clothing; divide the plunder of the enemies with your brothers."
verses.22:9: And the sons of Reuben, and the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned and departed from the sons of Israel from Shiloh, which is situated in Canaan, to enter Gilead, the land of their possession, which they had obtained according to the command of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
verses.22:10: And when they had come to the mounds of the Jordan in the land of Canaan, they built beside the Jordan an altar of immense size.
verses.22:11: And when the sons of Israel heard this, and reliable messengers had reported to them that the sons of Reuben, and of Gad, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar in the land of Canaan, upon the mounds of the Jordan, opposite the sons of Israel,
verses.22:12: they all gathered together at Shiloh to go up and fight against them.
verses.22:13: And meanwhile they sent to them into the land of Gilead Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest,
verses.22:14: and ten leaders with him, one from each tribe.
verses.22:15: They came to the sons of Reuben, and of Gad, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead, and said to them:
verses.22:16: "All the people of the Lord send this charge: 'What is this transgression? Why have you abandoned the Lord, the God of Israel, building a sacrilegious altar and departing from His worship?
verses.22:17: Is it too little for you that you sinned at Baal-peor, and to the present day the stain of this crime remains on us, and many of the people fell?
verses.22:18: And today you have abandoned the Lord, and tomorrow His wrath will rage against all Israel.
verses.22:19: Now if you think the land of your possession is unclean, cross over to the land in which the tabernacle of the Lord is, and dwell among us; only do not depart from the Lord and from our fellowship by building an altar besides the altar of the Lord our God.
verses.22:20: Did not Achan the son of Zerah transgress the commandment of the Lord, and His wrath descended upon all the people of Israel? And he was one man, and if only he alone had perished in his crime!'"
verses.22:21: Then the sons of Reuben, and of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the delegation of Israel:
verses.22:22: "The Most Mighty God, the Lord, the Most Mighty God, the Lord, He Himself knows, and Israel also will understand: if we have constructed this altar with an intent of treachery, let Him not protect us, but let Him punish us at this present time;
verses.22:23: and if we did it with the intention that we might place burnt offerings, and sacrifice, and peace offerings upon it, let Him Himself inquire and judge;
verses.22:24: and not rather with this thought and deliberation, so that we said, 'Tomorrow your sons will say to our sons, "What do you have to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?
verses.22:25: The Lord has set the Jordan River as a boundary between us and you, sons of Reuben and sons of Gad, and therefore you have no portion in the Lord." And through this occasion your sons will turn our sons away from the fear of the Lord.' Therefore we thought it better,
verses.22:26: and said, 'Let us construct an altar for ourselves, not for burnt offerings, nor for offering sacrificial victims,
verses.22:27: but as a witness between us and you, and our offspring and your descendants, so that we may serve the Lord, and that it may be our right to offer burnt offerings, and sacrificial victims, and peace offerings; and so that tomorrow your sons may never say to our sons, "You have no portion in the Lord."'
verses.22:28: And if they should choose to say that, they will answer them, 'Look, the altar of the Lord, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings, nor for sacrifice, but as a witness for us and for you.'
verses.22:29: Far be this crime from us, that we should depart from the Lord and abandon His footsteps by constructing an altar for offering burnt offerings, and sacrifices, and sacrificial victims, besides the altar of the Lord our God, which has been constructed before His tabernacle."
verses.22:30: Upon hearing these things, Phinehas the priest, and the leaders of the delegation of Israel who were with him, were appeased, and they most gladly accepted the words of the sons of Reuben, and of Gad, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.22:31: And Phinehas the priest, the son of Eleazar, said to them, "Now we know that the Lord is with us, because you are free from this treachery, and you have delivered the sons of Israel from the hand of the Lord."
verses.22:32: And he returned with the leaders from the sons of Reuben and Gad from the land of Gilead, of the borders of Canaan, to the sons of Israel, and reported to them.
verses.22:33: And the report pleased all who heard it. And the sons of Israel praised God, and no longer spoke at all of going up against them and fighting, and destroying the land of their possession.
verses.22:34: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad called the altar that they had constructed, "Our Witness, that the Lord Himself is God."
verses.23:1: Now after much time had passed, after the Lord had given peace to Israel, with all the surrounding nations subdued, and Joshua was now advanced in years and of extreme old age,
verses.23:2: Joshua summoned all Israel, and the elders, and the leaders and commanders, and the officers, and said to them, "I have grown old and am well along in years;
verses.23:3: and you see everything that the Lord your God has done to all the nations all around, how He Himself has fought for you.
verses.23:4: And now, because He has divided the whole land for you by lot, from the eastern side of the Jordan to the Great Sea, and many nations still remain,
verses.23:5: the Lord your God will destroy them and remove them from before your face, and you will possess the land, just as He promised you.
verses.23:6: Only be strong and be careful to keep everything that is written in the scroll of the law of Moses, and do not turn aside from them either to the right or to the left,
verses.23:7: so that after you have gone in to the nations who will be among you, you do not swear by the name of their gods, nor serve them, nor worship them,
verses.23:8: but cling to the Lord your God, which you have done until this day.
verses.23:9: And then the Lord God will remove in your sight great and very strong nations, and no one will be able to resist you.
verses.23:10: One of you will pursue a thousand men of the enemies, because the Lord your God Himself will fight for you, just as He promised.
verses.23:11: Take care most diligently for this alone, that you love the Lord your God.
verses.23:12: But if you choose to cling to the errors of these nations who dwell among you, and to join in marriage with them, and to form friendships,
verses.23:13: know right now that the Lord your God will not wipe them out before your face, but they will be a pit and a snare to you, and a stumbling block at your side, and stakes in your eyes, until He removes and destroys you from this excellent land, which He delivered to you.
verses.23:14: Look, today I am entering the way of all the earth, and you will know with your whole mind that of all the words that the Lord promised He would fulfill for you, not one has passed in vain.
verses.23:15: Therefore, just as He has fulfilled in deed what He promised, and all prosperous things have come, so He will bring upon you whatever evils He has threatened, until He removes and destroys you from this excellent land, which He delivered to you,
verses.23:16: because you have transgressed the covenant of the Lord your God, which He made with you, and have served foreign gods and worshiped them: quickly and swiftly the fury of the Lord will rise up against you, and you will be removed from this excellent land, which He delivered to you."
verses.24:1: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and called the elders, and the leaders, and the judges, and the officers; and they stood in the presence of the Lord,
verses.24:2: and he spoke to the people in this way: "This is what the Lord God of Israel says: 'Beyond the river your fathers lived from the beginning, Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor; and they served foreign gods.
verses.24:3: So I took your father Abraham from the borders of Mesopotamia, and brought him into the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed,
verses.24:4: and I gave him Isaac; and to him in turn I gave Jacob and Esau. Of these, to Esau I gave Mount Seir to possess; but Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.
verses.24:5: And I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with many signs and wonders.
verses.24:6: And I brought you and your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea; and the Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and cavalry, as far as the Red Sea.
verses.24:7: And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, who placed darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea upon them, and covered them. Your eyes saw everything that I did in Egypt, and you lived in the wilderness for a long time;
verses.24:8: and I brought you into the land of the Amorite, who lived beyond the Jordan. And when they fought against you, I handed them over into your hands, and you possessed their land, and killed them.
verses.24:9: Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. And he sent and called Balaam son of Beor, so that he might curse you;
verses.24:10: and I was unwilling to listen to him, but on the contrary, through him I blessed you, and I delivered you from his hand.
verses.24:11: And you crossed the Jordan, and came to Jericho. And the men of that city fought against you, the Amorite and the Perizzite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Girgashite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I handed them over into your hands.
verses.24:12: And I sent hornets before you, and I drove them out from their places, the two kings of the Amorites, not by your sword nor by your bow.
verses.24:13: And I gave you a land on which you did not labor, and cities that you did not build, so that you might live in them; vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.'
verses.24:14: So now fear the Lord, and serve Him with a whole and most true heart; and remove the gods that your fathers served in Mesopotamia and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.
verses.24:15: If, however, serving the Lord seems evil to you, the choice is given to you: choose today what pleases you, whom above all you ought to serve, whether the gods that your fathers served in Mesopotamia, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live; but I and my house will serve the Lord."
verses.24:16: And the people answered and said, "Far be it from us to abandon the Lord and serve foreign gods.
verses.24:17: The Lord our God, He Himself brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery; and He did mighty signs while we watched, and guarded us along the whole way by which we walked, and among all the peoples through whom we passed.
verses.24:18: And He drove out all the nations, the Amorite, the inhabitant of the land that we entered. Therefore we will serve the Lord, because He Himself is our God."
verses.24:19: And Joshua said to the people, "You will not be able to serve the Lord, for He is a holy God, strong and jealous; nor will He forgive your wicked deeds and sins.
verses.24:20: If you abandon the Lord and serve foreign gods, He will turn and afflict you and overthrow you, after He has granted good things to you."
verses.24:21: And the people said to Joshua, "By no means will it be as you say, but we will serve the Lord."
verses.24:22: And Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses that you yourselves have chosen the Lord for yourselves, to serve Him." And they answered, "Witnesses."
verses.24:23: "So now," he said, "remove the foreign gods from among you, and incline your hearts to the Lord God of Israel."
verses.24:24: And the people said to Joshua, "We will serve the Lord our God, and we will be obedient to His precepts."
verses.24:25: So Joshua made a covenant on that day, and set before the people precepts and ordinances in Shechem.
verses.24:26: He also wrote all these words in the scroll of the law of the Lord; and he took a very large stone, and placed it beneath the oak that was in the sanctuary of the Lord,
verses.24:27: and said to all the people, "Look, this stone will be a testimony to you, because it has heard all the words of the Lord that He spoke to you, so that afterward you may not wish to deny it and lie to the Lord your God."
verses.24:28: And he sent the people away, each to his own possession.
verses.24:29: And after these things Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being one hundred and ten years old;
verses.24:30: and they buried him within the borders of his possession in Timnath-serah, which is situated in Mount Ephraim, on the northern side of Mount Gaash.
verses.24:31: And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua and of the elders who lived a long time after Joshua, and who knew all the works of the Lord that He had done in Israel.
verses.24:32: Also, the bones of Joseph, which the sons of Israel had brought from Egypt, they buried in Shechem, in the portion of the field that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for one hundred young sheep; and it became the possession of the sons of Joseph.
verses.24:33: Eleazar son of Aaron also died, and they buried him in Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which was given to him in Mount Ephraim.

notes.1:6: The Vulgate reads 'sorte divides' ('divide by lot'), making the lottery allotment of the land explicit where the Hebrew reads simply 'cause to inherit.'
notes.1:7: The Vulgate renders this clause 'ut intelligas cuncta quæ agis' ('so that you may understand all that you do'), and similarly in 1:8 'diriges viam tuam, et intelliges eam' ('you will direct your way, and you will understand it'), where the Hebrew verb means 'act wisely' or 'prosper.'
notes.1:9: The Vulgate opens with an emphatic command, 'Ecce præcipio tibi' ('Look, I command you'), whereas the Hebrew poses a rhetorical question ('Have I not commanded you?').
notes.1:11: The Vulgate specifies 'post diem tertium' ('after the third day'), matching the three-day stay in 3:1-2, whereas the Hebrew reads 'within three days.'
notes.2:10: Here and in 2:11 the Vulgate reads 'ad vestrum introitum' / 'ad introitum vestrum' ('at your entry'), rendering the Hebrew preposition 'before you' or 'because of you' with a noun denoting Israel's arrival or approach.
notes.2:16: The Vulgate reads 'revertentes' ('those returning') rather than the Hebrew 'the pursuers.'
notes.2:18: The Vulgate connects 2:17 to 2:18 with 'si' ('if')—likely reading the Hebrew particle 'hinneh' ('look') as 'hen' ('if')—and adds 'signum' ('a sign'), stating the spies' discharge from the oath conditionally upon Rahab's compliance.
notes.2:23: The Vulgate opens with 'Quibus urbem ingressis' ('When those men had entered the city'), an explanatory transition absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.3:1: The Vulgate reads 'de nocte' ('in the night') instead of the Hebrew 'in the morning,' and ends with 'et morati sunt ibi tres dies' ('and they stayed there three days') rather than 'and lodged there before they crossed.'
notes.3:4: The Vulgate adds 'ut procul videre possitis' ('so that you may be able to see from a distance') and places the warning against approaching the ark at the end of the verse.
notes.3:16: The Vulgate depicts the waters as 'ad instar montis intumescentes' ('swelling up like a mountain'), reads 'from the city that is called Adam [Latin Adom] as far as the place Zarethan [Latin Sarthan]' (Hebrew: 'at Adam, the city beside Zarethan'), and identifies the lower sea as 'the Sea of the Wilderness (which is now called the Dead Sea)' rather than 'the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea.'
notes.3:17: The Vulgate describes the priests as 'accincti' (literally 'girded' or 'standing ready'), corresponding to the Hebrew 'firmly' or 'steadfastly.'
notes.4:3: Latin durissimos ("very hard") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Hebrew refers to the firmness of the priests' standing-place.
notes.4:5: Latin juxta numerum filiorum Israël ("according to the number of the sons of Israel") lacks the Hebrew's "tribes"; the same Vulgate reading recurs in 4:8.
notes.4:9: Latin Alios quoque duodecim lapides ("twelve other stones") explicitly distinguishes a second monument set in the riverbed from the twelve stones carried to Gilgal, whereas the Hebrew lacks the word "other."
notes.4:13: Latin per turmas, et cuneos ("by squadrons and columns") renders the armed vanguard using Roman military terms for cavalry squadrons and wedge formations, where the Hebrew simply describes troops equipped for battle.
notes.4:24: Native Vulgate Joshua 4:24 (the Red Sea comparison clause) maps to the second half of Saints.Bible 4:23, and native Vulgate 4:25 maps to Saints.Bible 4:24.
notes.5:4: Latin per longissimos viæ circuitus ("along the very long circuits of the way") expands the Hebrew phrase "on the way" to highlight the prolonged desert wanderings.
notes.5:11: Latin ejusdem anni ("of the same year")—paralleled by præsentis anni ("of the present year") in 5:12—is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew reads "on that very day."
notes.5:13: Latin in agro urbis Jericho ("in the field of the city of Jericho") specifies the open countryside outside the city, where the Hebrew reads simply "by Jericho."
notes.5:15: Native Vulgate Joshua 5:15 (Joshua's prostration) maps to Saints.Bible 5:14b, and native Vulgate 5:16 ('Solve, inquit...') maps to Saints.Bible 5:15.
notes.5:16: Native Vulgate numbers the commander's sandal command as 5:16 (mapping to Saints.Bible 5:15), following Joshua's prostration in native 5:15.
notes.6:5: Latin longior atque concisior ("longer and more broken") describes a prolonged trumpet blast combined with sharp, broken tones; funditus ("to their foundations") intensifies the collapse of the plural muri ("walls").
notes.6:6: Latin jubilæorum buccinas ("jubilee horns," echoed in 6:13) interprets the Hebrew rams' horns in terms of the jubilee year, distinct from tuba ("trumpet") in 6:5 and 6:20.
notes.6:17: Latin anathema (from Greek anathema, rendering Hebrew cherem) denotes persons or property irrevocably devoted to the Lord under a sacred ban of destruction.
notes.6:18: Latin de his, quæ præcepta sunt ("of these things that have been commanded") and sub peccato ("under sin") are Vulgate-distinct phrasings where the Hebrew speaks directly of taking from the devoted things and bringing the ban upon the camp.
notes.6:26: Latin In primogenito suo ... in novissimo liberorum ("In his firstborn ... in the youngest of his children") uses the Hebraizing price idiom rendered "At the cost of"; Latin suscitaverit ("raises up") also gives a transitive sense where the Hebrew reads "rises up."
notes.7:1: Latin anathema denotes spoils solemnly placed under the sacred ban and devoted to God for destruction; it is rendered consistently as "what was devoted to destruction" throughout the chapter. The Vulgate also specifies praevaricati sunt mandatum ("violated the command").
notes.7:7: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew verb as ut coepimus ("just as we began"), taking the root in the sense of "to begin" rather than "to be content."
notes.7:12: The Vulgate reads pollutus est anathemate ("has been defiled by what was devoted to destruction") and directs the judgment personally against "the one who is guilty of this crime" (eum qui hujus sceleris reus est; similarly in 7:13), where the Hebrew refers to the devoted thing itself.
notes.7:21: The Vulgate reads pallium coccineum ("a scarlet cloak") rather than the Hebrew "mantle from Shinar," and renders the gold object as regulam auream ("a golden bar").
notes.7:25: The Latin pairs turbasti ("you have troubled") with the intensive exturbet ("utterly trouble"), echoing the wordplay connected with the name of the Valley of Achor ("trouble").
notes.8:10: The Vulgate describes Joshua as vallatus auxilio pugnatorum ("surrounded by the support of fighting men"), using Roman military phrasing that incorporates the fighting force mentioned at the start of verse 11 in the Hebrew.
notes.8:13: Joshua is said to have "stood" (stetit) in the middle of the valley rather than "spent the night."
notes.8:18: The Vulgate reads clypeum ("shield") here and in 8:19, whereas the Hebrew has kidon ("javelin" or "short spear").
notes.8:26: The Clementine Vulgate reads clypeum ("shield") here.
notes.8:29: The Vulgate employs Roman execution terms, referring to the wooden structure first as patibulo ("gibbet") and then as cruce ("cross"), where the Hebrew uses the general word for "tree" or "wood" in both places.
notes.8:32: Latin "Deuteronomium" (borrowed from Greek) refers to a duplicate copy of the law of Moses.
notes.9:5: "As a sign of age" translates the Vulgate explanatory phrase "ad indicium vetustatis," which has no equivalent in the Hebrew; similarly, the Vulgate describes the loaves as "hard and crumbled into pieces" where the Hebrew reads "dry and crumbly."
notes.9:7: "In the land that is owed to us by lot" follows the distinctly Vulgate clause "in terra, quæ nobis sorte debetur," whereas the Hebrew reads, "Perhaps you live among us."
notes.9:16: "Would be among them" preserves the Vulgate future periphrastic ("inter eos futuri essent"), whereas the Hebrew states simply that they were living in their midst.
notes.10:12: "Do not move opposite Gibeon" reflects Vulgate "contra Gabaon ne movearis," whereas the Hebrew reads "be still at Gibeon."
notes.10:13: "The book of the just" translates the Vulgate plural "in libro justorum," corresponding to the Hebrew "Book of Jashar" ("the Upright").
notes.10:14: "So long a day" preserves Vulgate "tam longa dies" (Hebrew: "a day like it").
notes.10:40: "Ashdoth" (Latin Asedoth) preserves the Vulgate treatment of the Hebrew geographic common noun "ashedot" ("the slopes" or "foothills") as a proper place name.
notes.10:42: "Fought for him" reflects Vulgate "pugnavit pro eo" (Hebrew: "fought for Israel").
notes.11:6: Latin "vulnerandos" ("to be wounded") renders Hebrew "chalalim" ("pierced/killed"), where the Septuagint reads "put to flight."
notes.11:8: The Vulgate translates the second element of Hebrew "Misrephoth-maim" into Latin as "aquas Maserephoth" ("the waters of Misrephoth"), and shifts to the singular ("percussit ... dimitteret," referring to Joshua) where the Hebrew has the plural ("they struck").
notes.11:13: A distinctly Vulgate reading: Israel burned the other cities ("ceteras succendit Israël") apart from those on hills and mounds, and flame consumed Hazor alone, "the most strongly fortified" ("munitissimam," a Vulgate addition; "flamma" may be read as nominative "flame" or ablative "with flame"). By contrast, the Hebrew text states that Israel burned none of the cities standing on mounds except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.
notes.11:17: Latin "partem montis" ("the part of the mountain," and similarly "cujus pars" in 12:7) interprets Hebrew "hahar hechalaq" ("Mount Halak" or "the bare mountain") from the root meaning "portion/part." In 11:16, the Vulgate likewise renders Hebrew "ha'arabah" ("the Arabah") as "occidentalem plagam" ("the western region").
notes.11:20: The Vulgate uses distinctive judicial phrasing—"sententia" ("decree"), passive "indurarentur" ("should be hardened"), and "non mererentur ullam clementiam" ("not deserve any mercy")—where the Hebrew reads more briefly "it was from the Lord to harden their hearts ... so that they might receive no mercy."
notes.12:3: Latin "mare salsissimum" ("the Saltiest Sea") uses a superlative for Hebrew "yam hammelach" ("the Salt Sea"). Both here ("Asedoth, Phasga") and in 12:8 ("In Asedoth"), the Vulgate retains Hebrew "ashedoth" ("slopes") as a proper name, Ashdoth.
notes.12:8: The Clementine Vulgate attaches the first three geographical regions to the preceding sentence (v. 7) and begins a new sentence with the remaining three ("In Ashdoth, and in the wilderness, and in the south") linked to the nations by the verb "fuit" ("were"), whereas the Hebrew lists all six regions together.
notes.12:18: The Vulgate reads "Saron" ("Sharon"), treating the prefix of Hebrew "la-Sharon" as a preposition rather than part of the place name ("Lasharon").
notes.12:20: The Vulgate reads simply "Semeron" ("Shimron," as in 11:1), omitting the second element of Hebrew "Shimron-meron."
notes.12:22: The Clementine Vulgate distinctly reads "Jachanan Carmeli" ("Jachanan of Carmel"), where the Hebrew text has "Jokneam in Carmel" (rendered "Jecnam" in the Vulgate of 19:11 and 21:34). In 12:23, the Vulgate also translates Hebrew "Goiim" literally as "gentium" ("the nations of Gilgal").
notes.13:2: Vulgate renders Hebrew gelilot ("districts" or "regions") as the proper noun Galilæa ("Galilee"); although the Clementine text places a comma after Galilæa, Philisthiim functions as a genitive ("of the Philistines"), as in 13:3.
notes.13:3: Vulgate translates the river name Shihor descriptively as fluvio turbido ("the muddy river") and reads qui irrigat Ægyptum ("that waters Egypt") where the Hebrew has "which is east of Egypt."
notes.13:4: Vulgate reads Hevæi ("the Hivites") where the Hebrew has "the Avvim."
notes.13:5: Vulgate reads ejusque confinia ("and its borderlands") where the Hebrew has "the land of the Gebalites," connecting the name with the Hebrew word for "border."
notes.13:8: Latin cum qua ("with it") refers back to the half-tribe of Manasseh in 13:7, specifically meaning the eastern half-tribe alongside which Reuben and Gad received Transjordan.
notes.13:21: Vulgate renders the first Midianite prince as Hevæum ("Heveus," the Latin form of "Hivite") where the Hebrew has the personal name "Evi" (cf. Numbers 31:8).
notes.14:4: Vulgate explicitly writes in eorum successerunt locum ("succeeded to their place") to explain how Joseph's two tribes took Levi's territorial place, and renders the Hebrew for "their livestock and possessions" as jumenta et pecora sua ("their beasts of burden and their livestock").
notes.14:7: Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom "as it was in my heart" as quod mihi verum videbatur ("what seemed true to me").
notes.14:8: Here and in 14:9 and 14:14, Vulgate simply reads "followed the Lord" (secutus sum, secutus es, secutus est) without the Hebrew emphasis "wholly" or "fully."
notes.14:15: Reflecting an ancient tradition that Adam was buried at Hebron, Vulgate reads Hebrew ha-adam ("the man") as the proper name Adam and adds ibi ... situs est ("lies buried there").
notes.15:3: The Vulgate translates Hebrew Akrabbim ("scorpions") as the singular Latin Scorpionis ("of the Scorpion"), and similarly renders other place names into Latin in this chapter, including fons solis ("the Spring of the Sun") in 15:7 and Asor nova ("New Hazor") in 15:25.
notes.15:8: Whereas the Hebrew reads "the valley of Hinnom," the Vulgate transliterates the phrase as a single proper name, Geennom (rendered "Gehennom"), without repeating the word for "valley."
notes.15:9: The explanatory gloss "that is, the city of forests" (id est, urbs silvarum) is distinctive to the Vulgate and absent from the Hebrew text, parallel to the Vulgate gloss "that is, the city of letters" (id est, civitas litterarum) in 15:15.
notes.15:14: The Vulgate uses delevit ("wiped out/destroyed") where the Hebrew has "drove out," and in 15:17 explicitly includes junior ("younger") in describing Caleb's brother.
notes.15:18: The Vulgate diverges notably from the Hebrew here: Achsah is passively "persuaded by her husband" (suasa est a viro suo) rather than urging him, and she "sighed as she sat on the donkey" (suspiravitque ut sedebat in asino) rather than dismounting from it.
notes.15:52: The Vulgate reads Ruma ("Rumah"), reflecting a Hebrew textual variant with resh rather than the Masoretic reading "Dumah."
notes.15:60: As in 15:9, the Vulgate adds the explanatory gloss urbs silvarum ("the city of forests") after Kiriath-jearim, which is absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.15:63: The Vulgate uses the collective singular Jebusæum habitatorem ("the Jebusite, the inhabitant") and the verb delere ("to wipe out/destroy"), whereas the Hebrew has plural "inhabitants" and "drive out."
notes.16:2: Latin de Bethel Luza and terminum Archi, Ataroth omit directional prepositions (where Hebrew reads 'from Bethel to Luz' and 'the border of the Archites to Ataroth'), placing the names in apposition (cf. 18:13 identifying Luz with Bethel).
notes.16:3: Latin mari magno specifies 'the Great Sea' (the Mediterranean), whereas Hebrew has simply 'the sea.'
notes.16:8: Latin translates Hebrew Nahal Qanah ('Brook Kanah') as vallem arundineti ('the valley of the reed bed') and reads mare salsissimum ('the Saltiest Sea,' the Vulgate's usual name for the Dead Sea, cf. 18:19), whereas Hebrew reads simply 'to the sea' (the Mediterranean).
notes.16:10: Latin interfecerunt ('killed') differs from Hebrew horishu ('drove out' or 'dispossessed'), as also in 17:13.
notes.17:8: Latin quae est juxta terminos Manasse filiorum Ephraim attaches the relative pronoun to the town of Tappuah (Taphuae), using a genitive of possession (est ... filiorum Ephraim, 'belongs to the sons of Ephraim') to distinguish the town from its surrounding territory.
notes.17:9: Latin construes vallis arundineti ('of the valley of the reed bed') and civitatum Ephraim ('of the cities of Ephraim') as genitives modifying terminus and torrentis, whereas Hebrew reads 'to the brook of Kanah, south of the brook; these cities belong to Ephraim.'
notes.17:11: Latin et tertia pars urbis Nopheth ('and a third part of the city of Naphoth') renders Hebrew sheloshet han-nafet ('the three heights' or 'the third is Naphath') as a fraction of a city named Nopheth/Naphoth.
notes.17:12: Latin reads subvertere ('overthrow,' vs. Hebrew 'dispossess'), coepit ... habitare ('began to live,' vs. Hebrew 'persisted in living'), and in terra sua ('in his land,' vs. Hebrew 'in this land').
notes.17:16: Latin Non poterimus ad montana conscendere ('We will not be able to go up to the hill country') differs from Hebrew ('The hill country is not enough for us'); similarly in 17:18 Latin adds transibis ad montem and quem dicis ('who, you say').
notes.18:1: Latin tabernaculum testimonii ('the tabernacle of the testimony') renders Hebrew ohel mo'ed ('tent of meeting'), a frequent Vulgate translation.
notes.18:4: Latin reads juxta numerum uniuscujusque multitudinis ('according to the number of each one's multitude'), whereas Hebrew reads 'according to their inheritance'; similarly in 18:6 Latin specifies Mediam inter hos terram ('the middle land between these').
notes.18:11: Latin specifies sors prima ('the first lot') and uses a purpose clause (ut possiderent terram) where Hebrew has 'the lot of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin came up, and the border of their lot went out.'
notes.18:16: Latin has plural filiorum Ennom ('sons of Hinnom,' vs. Hebrew singular 'son of Hinnom') and includes an explanatory gloss (id est, vallem Ennom) after Geennom, just as it glosses Ensemes in 18:17 and Abenboen in 18:18.
notes.18:18: Latin translates Hebrew Gelilot as tumulos ('mounds') and ha-Aravah as campestria and planitiem ('plains' and 'plain'), and in 18:21 and 18:24 translates Hebrew Emek and Kefar as vallis ('valley') and villa ('village').
notes.19:11: Vulgate reads "from the sea" ("de mari"), whereas the Hebrew reads "westward" (lit. "toward the sea").
notes.19:13: Vulgate treats the Hebrew participle "ha-meto'ar" ("which bends/turns") as a distinct place name, "Amthar."
notes.19:15: Vulgate reads "Jerala" (reflecting an r/d consonant difference), whereas the Hebrew has "Idalah."
notes.19:29: Vulgate reads "Hormah" ("Horma") where the Hebrew has "Ramah," and renders Hebrew "chebel" ("region/cord") literally as "measuring line" ("funiculus," as also in v. 9).
notes.19:47: In the Clementine Vulgate, verses 47 and 48 are transposed relative to the Hebrew, so "And it is bounded by that very border" continues v. 46 (differing from Hebrew "the territory of the sons of Dan went out beyond them"). Vulgate also forms the compound name "Leshem Dan" where the Hebrew says they called Leshem "Dan."
notes.19:51: Vulgate renders Hebrew "tent of meeting" as "tabernacle of the testimony" ("tabernaculi testimonii"), and omits "finished" before "apportioned the land."
notes.20:2: Vulgate reads "cities of fugitives" ("urbes fugitivorum") rather than the Hebrew "cities of refuge."
notes.20:3: Vulgate explicitly adds "the wrath of the kinsman" ("iram proximi"), paraphrasing the Hebrew "avenger of blood" as "the kinsman who is the avenger of blood," and condenses Hebrew "unintentionally, without knowledge" into "unknowingly" ("nescius").
notes.20:9: Vulgate expands "avenger of blood" into "the kinsman desiring to avenge the shed blood," and reads "before the people to present his case" where the Hebrew has "before the congregation for judgment."
notes.21:9: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which uses an unspecified plural ("they gave"), the Vulgate names Joshua as the singular subject ("Joshua gave") and maintains singular verbs in vv. 12, 13, and 27.
notes.21:21: While v. 13 uses the singular for Hebron, the Vulgate renders "cities of refuge" in the plural here and in vv. 27, 32, 36, and 38, omitting the Hebrew qualifier "for the manslayer" that singles out only the first-named city.
notes.21:26: Here and in v. 34, the Vulgate renders the remaining non-priestly Levites as those "of the lower rank" (inferioris gradus), distinguishing them from the priestly sons of Aaron (cf. v. 5, "that is, the Levites who remained").
notes.21:27: The Vulgate reads Bosram ("Bosra," matching the Septuagint Bosoran) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Be-eshterah.
notes.21:36: In the Clementine Vulgate, v. 36 encompasses modern vv. 36-37 (and v. 38 encompasses vv. 38-39), includes "beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho," and lists Misor (from Hebrew mishor, "tableland/plain"), Jaser, and Jethson alongside Bezer and Mephaath where the Hebrew tradition lists Bezer, Jahaz, Kedemoth, and Mephaath.
notes.22:10: Vulgate "tumulos Jordanis" ("mounds of the Jordan") and "infinitae magnitudinis" ("of immense size") reflect Latin renderings distinct from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which speaks of the "districts" (gelilot) of the Jordan and an altar "imposing in appearance."
notes.22:17: Vulgate uses the proper name "Beelphegor" ("Baal-peor") and speaks of "the stain of this crime" remaining on Israel, whereas the Hebrew text reads simply "the iniquity of Peor" from which Israel has not cleansed itself.
notes.22:20: Vulgate reads "atque utinam solum periisset" ("and if only he alone had perished"), taking the underlying Hebrew particle as an optative wish rather than the negative statement ("that man did not perish alone") of the Masoretic Text.
notes.22:32: Vulgate has the genitive apposition "de terra Galaad, finium Chanaan" ("from the land of Gilead, of the borders of Canaan"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan."
notes.22:34: Vulgate gives the altar the explicit name "Testimonium nostrum, quod Dominus ipse sit Deus" ("Our Witness, that the Lord Himself is God"), whereas the Hebrew text leaves the name itself unstated before explaining that it is a witness between the tribes.
notes.23:4: Vulgate reads third-person "divisit" ("He has divided") with the Lord as subject and specifies "from the eastern side of the Jordan," whereas the Hebrew text has Joshua speaking in the first person ("I have allotted") without "eastern side."
notes.23:9: Vulgate renders the verbs in the future tense ("auferet ... poterit", "will remove ... will be able to resist") introduced by "Et tunc" ("And then"), turning the Hebrew past-tense summary of victories into a conditional future promise.
notes.23:12: Vulgate reads "erroribus adhaerere" ("to cling to the errors") of these peoples, whereas the Hebrew text speaks of clinging to the "remnant" of these nations.
notes.23:13: Vulgate renders the images of judgment as "a stumbling block at your side, and stakes in your eyes" ("offendiculum ... sudes"), where the Hebrew text speaks of a "scourge" on the sides and "thorns" in the eyes.
notes.24:3: The Vulgate explicitly names Mesopotamia (de Mesopotamiae finibus here, and in Mesopotamia in vv. 14-15), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "beyond the River" (the Euphrates).
notes.24:5: The Vulgate reads "with many signs and wonders" (multis signis atque portentis), whereas the Hebrew reads "according to what I did in its midst, and afterward I brought you out."
notes.24:15: The Vulgate adds "the choice is given to you" (optio vobis datur) and expands the Hebrew "choose for yourselves today whom you will serve" to "choose today what pleases you, whom above all you ought to serve."
notes.24:29: Native Vulgate Joshua 24:29-31 place Joshua's death and burial in 24:29-30 and Israel's continued service in 24:31, matching the Hebrew order (mapping to Saints.Bible Septuagint-aligned order 24:30-31 and 24:29).
notes.24:31: In native Clementine Vulgate order, Joshua's death and burial stand at 24:29-30 (Saints.Bible 24:30-31) and Israel's continued service stands at 24:31 (Saints.Bible 24:29).
notes.24:32: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate renders the purchase price as "one hundred young sheep" (centum novellis ovibus), where the Hebrew has "one hundred qesitahs" (an ancient unit of weight or money); in v. 33 the Vulgate similarly treats Gabaath (Gibeah) as a proper place name rather than the common noun "hill."
